commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kernel] Extend skinny gemm N=5 to N=8 cases on GFX12 (RDNA4) using  SWMMAC optimization
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR adds an optimized ROCm GFX12 (RDNA4) SWMMAC-based skinny GEMM path.

The new path targets serving workloads with low max concurrency, matching the benchmarked decode GEMM range of N=5-8. The implementation uses sparse wave matrix multiply-accumulate instructions on GFX12 (RDNA4) to improve throughput for these skinny GEMM cases, while keeping the existing fallback path for unsupported cases.

Skinny GEMMs can be important for ROCm/GFX12 (RDNA4) serving performance, which is often used in local or small-scale serving setups. In these deployments, the server is expected to handle single users, or a small number of users with a relatively lower request rate, so the active decode batch can remain small instead of being filled to a large batch size.

This optimization follows the same general direction described in the Hugging Face technical blog, [*Creating custom kernels for the AMD MI300*](https://huggingface.co/blog/mi300kernels). The blog discusses custom kernels for AMD MI300X vLLM serving and describes a skinny GEMM optimization for inputs with 8 or fewer rows.

The key idea is to map each logical skinny A row into two adjacent SWMMAC sparse rows. The first sparse row selects one set of 16-bit pairs from `A[n, :]`, and the second sparse row selects the complementary pairs from the same logical row. Both sparse rows multiply with the same normal `B[32 x 16]` fragment, producing two partial accumulator rows. The epilogue then adds the adjacent partial rows back together to recover the final logical output row. This interleaved sparse-row layout lets the kernel use the SWMMAC instruction shape more effectively for N=5-8 instead of leaving the skinny rows underfilled.

A related optimization direction is also being explored in IREE: [*[AMDGPU][Codegen] Optimizing skinny GEMM workloads with sparse matrix instructions*](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/22863). The IREE issue describes using sparse matrix instructions to optimize skinny GEMM workloads on AMD CDNA GPUs. Although the IREE discussion focuses on IREE codegen and CDNA-style sparse MFMA examples, the motivation is closely related: skinny GEMM workloads can waste matrix instruction capacity due to padding or under-filled dimensions, and sparse matrix instructions can recover more effective throughput.

Note: this PR is not a direct port of either implementation. It adapts the same idea to the vLLM ROCm/GFX12 (RDNA4) path using SWMMAC with tuned optimization strategies for the measured small-N decode GEMM cases.

**This PR:**

* Adds a GFX12 (RDNA4) SWMMAC skinny GEMM kernel path
* Targets decode GEMM shapes with N=5-8
* Preserves the existing fallback path for unsupported cases
* Adds correctness coverage for the new SWMMAC path across:

  * N = 5, 6, 7, 8
  * FP16 and BF16, matching the existing skinny GEMM dtype coverage
  * Multiple M/K sizes
  * Aligned (divisible by 16) and non-aligned M dimensions 
  * Large-shape cases

Note: N=4 was also evaluated, but it did not show a benefit in this implementation, so this PR keeps the optimized path scoped to N=5-8.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_skinny_gemms.py::test_rocm_swmmac_gemm_kernel
```

### GSM8K end-to-end accuracy

The GSM8K run was performed with the vLLM server launched using --max-num-seqs 8, and lm_eval used num_concurrent=8. This keeps the active decode batch within the targeted skinny GEMM range and exercises the SWMMAC N=5-8 paths.

**Model:** `Qwen/Qwen3-4B`

Server command:
```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
  ```

Benchmark command:
```bash
lm_eval \
  --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=${MODEL},base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=8,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=1024,max_length=8192,timeout=60000" \
  --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --output_path ./results_qwen3_4b_gsm8k \
  --log_samples
```


### Performance Benchmark

- **Hardware:** GPU: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201, GFX12 (RDNA4), **x1** | CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-Core Processor, **x32**  |  RAM: 123Gi
- **Model:** Qwen/Qwen3-4B
- **Benchmark setup:**
  - **Concurrency:** 5, 6, 7, 8
  - **Input/output token shapes:** 512/128, 1024/256, 2048/128, 2048/512, 4096/512, 8192/512, 1024/2048, 512/4096, 512/8192

Baseline commit (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/6bdabbad5bce747865fd3a249658518a4269cc22):

```text
commit 6bdabbad5bce747865fd3a249658518a4269cc22
Author: Jee Jee Li <[pandaleefree@gmail.com](mailto:pandaleefree@gmail.com)>
Date:   Sun May 31 13:16:12 2026 +0800

    Signed-off-by: Jee Jee Li <[jeejeelee@inferact.ai](mailto:jeejeelee@inferact.ai)>
```

Server script:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

rm -rf ~/.cache/vllm

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
  --dtype auto \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
```

Benchmark script:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

BASE_URL=${BASE_URL:-http://localhost:8000}
RESULT_DIR=${RESULT_DIR:-./bench-results}
RESULT_PREFIX=${RESULT_PREFIX:-qwen3-4b}
CONCURRENCIES=${CONCURRENCIES:-"5 6 7 8"}
NUM_WARMUPS=${NUM_WARMUPS:-16}

for workload in \
  "512 128" \
  "1024 256" \
  "2048 512" \
  "4096 512" \
  "8192 512" \
  "2048 128" \
  "1024 2048" \
  "512 4096" \
  "512 8192"; do

  set -- $workload

  OUTPUT_LEN=$2

    vllm bench serve \
      --backend openai-chat \
      --base-url "${BASE_URL}" \
      --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
      --model Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
      --dataset-name random \
      --input-len "${INPUT_LEN}" \
      --output-len "${OUTPUT_LEN}" \
      --num-prompts "${NUM_PROMPTS}" \
      --request-rate inf \
      --max-concurrency "${C}" \
      --num-warmups "${NUM_WARMUPS}" \
      --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
      --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 \
      --save-result \
      --result-dir "${RESULT_DIR}" \
      --result-filename "${RESULT_PREFIX}-${INPUT_LEN}-${OUTPUT_LEN}-C${C}.json" \
      --metadata model=qwen3-4b concurrency="${C}" workload=random_${INPUT_LEN}_${OUTPUT_LEN} num_prompts="${NUM_PROMPTS}"
  done
done
```


## Test Results

### Unit tests
216 passed, 16 warnings in 52.55s

### GSM8K end-to-end accuracy

| Version | flexible-extract exact_match | strict-match exact_match | Request progress |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Baseline** | 0.8613 ± 0.0095 | 0.8650 ± 0.0094 | 1319 requests in 11:13, 1.96 it/s |
| **SWMMAC** | 0.8605 ± 0.0095 | 0.8666 ± 0.0094 | 1319 requests in 09:48, 2.24 it/s |

commits.pr_title: [XPU][batch invariant] Optimize batch-invariant collectives with sharded reductions
commits.pr_body:
Use all-to-all and fused Triton summation for inputs above 4 MiB, followed by all-gather for all-reduce. Keep the existing all-gather path for smaller inputs and uneven reduce-scatter during graph capture.

Keep gather and sharded all-reduce implementations separate, with explicit dispatch at the entry point. Accumulate in FP32 on both paths and cast back to the input dtype once.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Add DSpine support
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Add DSpine speculative decoding for Qwen, based on [Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36173) and the [Tencent reference implementation](https://github.com/Tencent/DSpine). - Supports Tencent and Speculators checkpoint layouts through one model implementation. - Reuses existing candidate sampling and verification; DSpine supplies its candidate transition scores. - Adds a Qwen3.8-27B GSM8K regression to the existing DFlash test suite and CI configuration. The implementation extends the existing DFlash/DFlash2 paths with checkpoint-format adaptation and TP-aware transition scoring, without adding a separate sampling implementation. ## Validation Evaluated `tencent/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16` with `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` on **one H100 80GB**, BF16, TP=1, FA3, concurrency 8, and **15 draft tokens**. The five-dataset acceptance runs use **thinking enabled**, `reasoning_effort=xhigh`, a 4,096-token output cap, and no prefix caching. T0 uses greedy drafts; T1 uses probabilistic drafts with target sampling `top_p=0.95, top_k=20`. Each result below is **mean per-response acceptance length / pooled acceptance length**. | Dataset | Responses per run | T0 | T1 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | GSM8K | 1,319 | 6.9271 / 5.9024 | 6.4762 / 5.4559 | | MATH-500 | 500 | 6.3780 / 5.1225 | 5.8710 / 4.6984 | | HumanEval | 164 | 5.7120 / 5.2160 | 5.1886 / 4.6133 | | MBPP | 500 | 5.9092 / 5.1499 | 5.4030 / 4.6400 | | MT-Bench | 160 | 4.6933 / 4.1340 | 4.3010 / 3.7483 | The acceptance numbers below were measured with draft revision `5f54174d301dbca65d9aa4448dc47e56732d9a12`. The server command uses the [updated Hugging Face revision](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16/tree/260a6c23070ca873ff1a5f33b7119ac3f6a245ee), which declares `DSpineDraftModel` in its config.
Start the T1 server from the vLLM checkout ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --revision 37561816e66b5b9153b1b64c10968c18c1e6f4a0 \ --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18481 \ --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --language-model-only \ --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --generation-config vllm --seed 0 \ --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASH_ATTN","flash_attn_version":3}' \ --speculative-config '{ "model":"tencent/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16", "revision":"260a6c23070ca873ff1a5f33b7119ac3f6a245ee", "method":"dflash", "num_speculative_tokens":15, "enable_adaptive_verification":false, "draft_sample_method":"probabilistic" }' \ --per-request-spec-decode-metrics summary ```
Once the server is ready, run from the Speculators checkout with its evaluation dependencies installed:
Run the T1 GSM8K acceptance evaluation ```bash python /home/shanjiaz/dspine-evaluations/tencent-b16-acceptance-aiperf-20261110/speculators-checkout/scripts/evaluate/evaluate.py \ acceptance \ --dataset gsm8k \ --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --tokenizer Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --tokenizer-revision 37561816e66b5b9153b1b64c10968c18c1e6f4a0 \ --url http://127.0.0.1:18481 \ --num-conversations 1319 \ --concurrency 8 \ --extra-inputs '{"temperature": 1, "max_completion_tokens": 4096, "reasoning_effort": "xhigh", "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true}, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20}' \ --output-artifact-dir /home/shanjiaz/dspine-evaluations/tencent-b16-probabilistic-aiperf-20261111/t1-gsm8k ```
Tested higher concurrency with adaptive verification on/off on 8 h100s: ## Note **Weight loading:** Tencent stacks independent layer matrices in shared checkpoint tensors; we unpack them into per-layer `ReplicatedLinear` modules and map names through the existing DFlash loader, preserving the learned values and using the same model implementation for both checkpoint layouts. AI assistance was used in implementation and validation. ---

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes the `:nvidia: (B200) [Nightly] Fusion E2E Config Sweep` failure tracked in #67307. `test_tp1_fp4_mixed_precision_act_fusion[...Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4...]` started failing after #67693 changed the dummy FP8 weights. This PR moves #67753's narrow dummy FP8 fixture into `tests/conftest.py` as `narrow_dummy_fp8_weights`, and uses it in both the HiSparse tests and this fusion test.

## Root cause

- The test loads the model with `load_format="dummy"`. It compares the fused (`silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant`) and unfused NVFP4 MLP outputs with `assert_close(atol=1e-1, rtol=1e-1)`. The two paths are not bitwise equal: the unfused path rounds the SiLU output to bf16 before quantizing, so a few elements land one FP4 step apart.
- Since #67693, `initialize_single_dummy_weight` fills every 8-bit float param with random codes across the FP8 range. Dense NVFP4 linears (`KNvfp4Static`) store their block scales `weight_scale` as `float8_e4m3fn`, without the positive `dummy_weight_value` that the NVFP4 MoE path sets. So these scales are now signed and up to ±448, where they used to be within ±1.
- The larger activations turn that one-step rounding difference into large absolute errors. Nightly [102861](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102861): 103 / 5120 elements mismatch, greatest absolute difference 1.41. The test passed in nightly 102740, before #67693 merged.

## Changes

- `tests/conftest.py`: new `narrow_dummy_fp8_weights` fixture. It is the #67753 patch (8-bit float dummy weights default to `low=-1, high=1`). It also sets `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`, because a monkeypatch only reaches an engine in the pytest process.
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: replaces the local autouse fixture with `pytestmark = pytest.mark.usefixtures("narrow_dummy_fp8_weights")`. All HiSparse tests already set `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`, so they behave as before.
- `tests/compile/fusions_e2e/test_tp1_quant.py`: `test_tp1_fp4_mixed_precision_act_fusion` uses the fixture. It is TP1, so with the engine core in process the model runs in the pytest process, and the patch applies.

## Validation

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (v0.17.2, the pre-commit pin) and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Not yet run on a GPU.** The fusion test needs Blackwell. It runs only in the B200 nightly Fusion E2E Config Sweep step. The HiSparse change only moves code.

## Alternative considered

Giving dense NVFP4 block scales a positive `dummy_weight_value`, as the MoE path does, would fix the root cause for every dummy NVFP4 dense model. It changes dummy-loader behaviour for benchmarks, though, so it is left for a separate discussion with the #67693 author.

## Overview

Routes per-tensor FP8 linear layers (static activation scales) to AITER's Triton `gemm_a8w8` for decode batches of 5 to 256 tokens, on shapes AITER has tuned configs for. Everything else keeps the current `ROCmFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` path.

## Claims

Llama 3.1 8B FP8 on MI355X (gfx950):

- **Decode is faster:** at 1k/1k, concurrency 16–256, TPOT is 1.3–8.1% lower and total token throughput is 1.3–8.4% higher. At 8k/1k, concurrency 16 has 6.1% lower TPOT and 9.5% higher throughput; concurrency 32–256 moves the same way but within run-to-run noise.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Guard cross-node symmetric-memory rendezvous
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Cross-node symmetric-memory rendezvous is safe only when every rank belongs to
the same NVLink fabric. Without a topology check, unsupported groups can hang
or fail during CUDA memory import. This affects generic symmetric-memory
all-reduce as well as Direct DCP, custom all-reduce, Async TP, GEMM RS/AR, and
the Kimi K3 latent-MoE tail fusion.

This change:

- classifies groups as `INTRA_NODE`, `CROSS_NODE_NVLINK`, or `UNSUPPORTED`;
- reads the fabric UUID and clique ID through vLLM's vendored NVML V2 API
  (`c_nvmlGpuFabricInfoV_t` and `nvmlDeviceGetGpuFabricInfoV`), without spawning
  `nvidia-smi`;
- fails closed when fabric metadata is absent, invalid, or differs across
  ranks;
- applies the topology guard before entering symmetric-memory rendezvous; and
- prevents forced Direct DCP settings from bypassing topology safety.

The legacy `nvmlDeviceGetGpuFabricInfo` structure is not compatible with the
GB300 driver used for validation: it exposed zero clique/state fields. The versioned
V2 call returns correct UUID and clique.

AI assistance was used.

## Test Plan

- Run `git diff --check` and pre-commit on both changed files.
- Run `tests/distributed/test_nvlink_fabric.py` in the GB300 validation image.
- On H100, B200, and GB300 clusters, allocate two nodes, then
  launch eight ranks (four GPUs per node) against exact baseline and patched
  source snapshots using PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`.
- For each topology, inspect raw NVLink fabric metadata, exercise Direct CP in
  forced and automatic modes, initialize `SymmMemCommunicator`, and validate a
  BF16 all-reduce. Each potentially unsafe stage has a 180-second timeout.
- On GB300, test both two nodes within one NVL72 group and two nodes from
  different NVL72 groups.

No model evaluation was run: the change affects collective selection rather
than model numerics. Collective correctness was checked on all eight ranks;
the expected and observed BF16 sum was 36.

## Test Result

| Hardware / topology | Before | Topology after | Direct CP after | Symmetric memory after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100, cross-node | Forced Direct CP was enabled; generic symmetric-memory rendezvous timed out. | `UNSUPPORTED` (null fabric UUID) | **Disabled** in forced and automatic modes | **Disabled**; NCCL fallback correct on 8/8 ranks |
| B200, cross-node | Forced Direct CP was enabled; generic symmetric-memory rendezvous timed out. | `UNSUPPORTED` (null fabric UUID) | **Disabled** in forced and automatic modes | **Disabled**; NCCL fallback correct on 8/8 ranks |
| B200, single-node | Regression check added for this change. | `INTRA_NODE` (null fabric UUID is irrelevant) | **Enabled** in forced and automatic modes | **Enabled**; symmetric-memory all-reduce correct on 4/4 ranks |
| GB300, same NVL72 | Direct CP and symmetric memory both worked. | `CROSS_NODE_NVLINK` (one shared UUID/clique) | **Enabled** in forced and automatic modes | **Enabled**; symmetric-memory all-reduce correct on 8/8 ranks |
| GB300, different NVL72 groups | Forced Direct CP was enabled; symmetric-memory initialization logged `invalid resource handle`. | `UNSUPPORTED` (two fabric UUIDs) | **Disabled** in forced and automatic modes | **Disabled**; NCCL fallback correct on 8/8 ranks |

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Enable encoder graph capture for Kimi-K3 Vision Tower
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Implements `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` for `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration` on AMD ROCm (MI355X), so the Kimi-K3 vision tower (`MoonViT3dPretrainedModel` + `KimiK25MultiModalProjector`) can be replayed from captured graphs via `cudagraph_mm_encoder=True`.

An earlier revision of this PR also added `torch.compile` for the vision tower (`compile_mm_encoder`). That part was dropped after review (thanks @simondanielsson): profiling showed Inductor fuses only norms, residual adds and GELU (full tower 301 -> 275 kernels, about 1% of GPU time), because GEMMs, AITER FMHA and `packed_qk_rope` (about 94% of time) are opaque kernels. The gain comes from graph replay, not fusion.

Related PRs and why this is not a duplicate:

- #53011: avoids eager `torch.compile` in the Kimi K2.5 vision helper (bugfix, not encoder cudagraphs).
- #44394 and #56820: add encoder CUDA graph support for other models (PaddleOCR-VL, Ling-3.0-flash-VL) on the same `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` interface. This PR only implements the interface for Kimi-K3.

No other open PR implements `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` for Kimi-K3. 

## Changes

- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/encoder_cudagraph.py`: `KimiK3EncoderCudaGraphMixin` (item specs, item selection, capture inputs, replay buffers, graph and eager forwards). Auto-inferred budgets are capped at 512 tokens; larger inputs use the existing eager path of `EncoderCudaGraphManager`. See [discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63086#discussion_r4440377966) .
- `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py`: test correctness of graph-vs-eager and token cap limit

The feature is opt-in (`cudagraph_mm_encoder`, default off); default behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

### Encoder-level profile (MI355X, full vision tower, 512x512 image)

Wall time per encoder call: eager 7.1 ms, cudagraph replay 4.5 ms. The kernel list is identical; the gain is removed launch overhead and idle gaps between small kernels, so it is largest for small images. Full traces and kernel breakdown: see the profiling section already posted in this description.

### Serving (MI355X, TP=8, 9-point sweep, 3 repetitions per configuration, default config)

A = eager vision tower. D = `cudagraph_mm_encoder=true` only, no manual overrides — budgets auto-infer to `[64, 128, 256, 512]`, i.e. just turning the flag on. Interleaved A/D/A/D/A/D, fresh server boot each. One point, `768x1024`, sits above the 512-token cap so it runs eagerly under D too — a neutral control for the cutoff.

Result: speedup visible both at the serving level and encoder profile.

Note on noise: each sweep point runs 96 prompts (3 reps = ~5h GPU compute), and only one point (256x256 @ conc=16, mean TTFT -13.35%) individually clears the noise band — every other point is inside noise on its own. That's expected: the vision tower runs once per prompt (one image per prompt), so it's a small slice of total request cost, and a clear per-call win in the encoder microbenchmark (7.1ms eager -> 4.5ms graphed) shows up as a small, only-geomean-resolvable gain at the serving level. The geomean (not any single point) is the evidence for a real effect.

| metric | D vs A (geomean) | noise floor |
|---|---|---|
| Mean TTFT | -3.92% ± 1.60 | ≤4.0%/point — reliable |
| Median TTFT | -0.87% ± 5.39 | up to 25%/point — directional only |
| Throughput | +3.12% ± 1.85 | ≤7.7%/point |
| TPOT | -2.83%/-2.11% | expected flat; within noise, decode path untouched |

Above-cap control (`768x1024`, eager under D): throughput +2.71%, mean TTFT +3.30% — flat/noisy as expected, confirms traffic above the cutoff isn't regressed.

- ROCm only; the NVIDIA model is unchanged. Deduplicating the encoder-graph methods between `amd/model.py` and `nvidia/model.py` into a common mixin is planned as a follow-up PR once this merges.
- Default auto-inferred budgets are capped at 512 tokens; larger inputs run eagerly. See [discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63086#discussion_r4440377966)
- Serving statistics: 3 repetitions on a single node, 96 prompts/point (32 at conc=1/4, 256 at conc=64), fixed seeds per point. Geomean deltas are reliable (stdev ≤1.9%); per-point deltas are noisier — below ~4% for mean TTFT, ~8% for throughput/TPOT, ~25% for median TTFT isn't distinguishable from noise. The vision tower runs once per prompt, so a real per-call improvement is a small fraction of total request time and only resolves at the geomean level, not per point.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Drop the stale config read from the FlashInfer indexer builder
commits.pr_body:
## Overview `MiniMaxM3IndexerFlashInferMetadataBuilder` (added in #66018) still reads the legacy `text_config.sparse_attention_config` dict, which the upstream `MiniMaxM3VLTextConfig` adopted in #61813 no longer exposes. Constructing the builder raises `AttributeError` on SM90 and SM120/SM121, where the FlashInfer MSA indexer is selected. This PR removes that read. ## Claims - The FlashInfer indexer builder constructs again with the upstream MiniMax-M3 config. - `test_flashinfer_indexer_impl_matches_triton` passes again on SM121 (it fails on `main`). - No behavior change otherwise: `local_blocks` comes from the same config field, through the impl instead of the builder. ## Validation DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, driver 580.178.04), `main` at 6d3eba027 (the two touched files are unchanged at 1c675c6868), precompiled cu132 wheel, torch 2.14.0, flashinfer 0.7.3, transformers 5.22.2. ```bash pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py -k flashinfer_indexer -v pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py pre-commit run --files vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/indexer_flashinfer.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py ``` `-k flashinfer_indexer`: | tree | result | |---|---| | `main` | 4 failed, `common/indexer.py:255`: `'Qwen3Config' object has no attribute 'index_n_heads'` (stale test setup) | | `main` + the test change | 4 failed, `indexer_flashinfer.py:78`: `'Qwen3Config' object has no attribute 'sparse_attention_config'` | | this PR | 4 passed | | this PR with `force_end = 0` | 2 failed (the `local_blocks=1` cases), 2 passed, so the test covers the value now taken from the impl | Whole file with this PR: 166 passed, 103 skipped. `pre-commit`: passed. With the `config.json` of `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` and `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` loaded through `get_config`, on the same GPU `minimax_m3_use_flashinfer_msa` passes and `select_indexer_impl_cls` returns `MiniMaxM3IndexerFlashInferImpl` for bf16 and fp8 index caches. Constructing its builder fails on `main` with ``` AttributeError: 'MiniMaxM3VLTextConfig' object has no attribute 'sparse_attention_config' ``` and succeeds with this PR. End to end on the same GPU: a tiny dummy-weight MiniMax-M3 (the config from `tests/models/minimax_m3/test_index_cache_overrides.py`, which is ROCm-only) started through `LLM(..., load_format="dummy")`, two 2304-token prompts, 4 greedy tokens each. | tree | result | |---|---| | `main` | engine does not start: `create_metadata_builders` -> `indexer_flashinfer.py:78` -> `AttributeError: 'MiniMaxM3VLTextConfig' object has no attribute 'sparse_attention_config'` -> `Engine core initialization failed` | | this PR | engine starts, logs `MiniMax M3 indexer: selected FlashInfer MSA (proxy score + top-k)`, and generates for both prompts | The script passes `attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}` for the dense layers, because FLASH_ATTN from the cu132 wheel does not load on this machine's 580 driver (#67177). That is unrelated to this change.
e2e_m3_dummy.py (run as python e2e_m3_dummy.py TRITON_ATTN) ```python """End-to-end engine start + generation for a tiny dummy-weight MiniMax-M3 (same recipe as tests/models/minimax_m3/test_index_cache_overrides.py, which is ROCm-only), to reach the FlashInfer indexer builder on this GPU.""" import math import sys import tempfile from transformers import MiniMaxM3VLConfig from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="m3tiny-") MiniMaxM3VLConfig( architectures=["MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM"], text_config={ "num_hidden_layers": 5, "hidden_size": 128, "dense_intermediate_size": 256, "num_attention_heads": 1, "num_key_value_heads": 1, "head_dim": 128, "vocab_size": 256, "bos_token_id": 1, "eos_token_id": 2, "max_position_embeddings": 4096, "mlp_layer_types": ["dense"] * 5, "layer_types": ["full_attention"] * 3 + ["minimax_m3_sparse"] * 2, "index_n_heads": 1, }, ).save_pretrained(tmp) if __name__ == "__main__": extra = {} if len(sys.argv) > 1: extra["backend"] = sys.argv[1] llm = LLM( tmp, load_format="dummy", skip_tokenizer_init=True, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=4096, block_size=128, max_num_seqs=1, max_num_batched_tokens=4096, kv_cache_memory_bytes=64 * 1024 * 1024, enforce_eager=True, enable_prefix_caching=False, attention_config={"indexer_kv_dtype": "bf16", **extra}, generation_config="vllm", ) for offset in (0, 37): tokens = [3 + (i + offset) % 250 for i in range(2304)] out = llm.generate( [{"prompt_token_ids": tokens}], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=4, ignore_eos=True, logprobs=5), use_tqdm=False, )[0].outputs[0] vals = [p.logprob for row in out.logprobs for p in row.values()] assert len(out.token_ids) == 4 and all(math.isfinite(v) for v in vals) print("E2E_GENERATED offset", offset, "token_ids", list(out.token_ids)) print("E2E_OK") ```
Not run: a released checkpoint. They are 252-854 GB (172 GB for the smallest quantized one I found), more than the 121 GB of this machine. SM90 was not tested. The end-to-end run uses dummy weights, so no eval was run; the change does not alter model output. ## Details `MiniMaxM3VLTextConfig.__post_init__` pops `sparse_attention_config` and maps it to flat `index_*` fields, so the attribute does not exist on a loaded config. #66018 was opened before #61813 merged and landed after it, which is how the legacy read got in. The impl already receives `local_blocks` from the model (`local_blocks=config.index_local_blocks`), which is what the MSA and Triton indexers use. `forward` now uses `self.local_blocks`, and the builder's copy is removed (`__init__`, the metadata field, two imports). The test sets `index_n_heads` instead of the legacy dict. CI did not catch this: `test_flashinfer_indexer_impl_matches_triton` needs SM90 or SM120/SM121, and the steps that run this file use L4 and B200 (skipped) or H100 with `-k prefill_sparse_attention_correctness` (deselected). The second commit adds the test to that H100 step's `-k` filter and lists `common/indexer.py` and `nvidia/indexer_flashinfer.py` as its dependencies. I could not run it on SM90, so this PR's own H100 run is the first check of that path; on SM121 the new filter selects 8 tests and all pass. Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR mentions `indexer_flashinfer` or this `AttributeError` (searched 2026-11-12), and #66018 has no follow-up commits. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, tests, and review. The human submitter reviewed the changes and authorized submission. The validation results above were obtained with AI assistance. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

commits.pr_title: [MoE] Disable expanded DeepEP v2 dispatch in all execution modes
commits.pr_body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This PR is a duplicate of and supersedes #59337.** It is opened from
> `neuralmagic/vllm` because the original PR branch is in a fork where the
> submitter does not have write access. The original description, rationale
> and validation history are copied below, followed by validation on the
> replacement branch.

## Replacement Branch Update

Current head `47ba135367d78e666d25daa2c322e2f5f1d7369b` includes merge
`c6f2e79c6b` with `origin/main` at `9ad0029883` and the final
`test_moe.py` receiver-signature compatibility fix.

- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed for all seven changed files, including
  Ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX, test-tethering and docstring checks;
  `git diff --check` also passed.
- Full DeepEP v2 test set: **1548 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed**. The 16 skips
  require FlashInfer TRTLLM on SM100; validation used H200/SM90 GPUs.
- DeepEP v2 async-finalize suite in the requested environment with NCCL 2.30.7:
  **6 passed**.
- Previously failing `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py` set on two H200 GPUs:
  **191 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed** (891 deselected; 2m45s).

## Purpose

DeepEP v2 currently selects expanded dispatch and CPU synchronization from `enforce_eager`. Use `do_expand=False` and `do_cpu_sync=False` for every forward so eager execution, warmup and CUDA graph capture share the same dispatch contract.

Remove the constructor flag and unused expanded-layout receiver code. Preserve DP-wide, sequence-parallel-aware receive-capacity buckets, padding masking and GPU receive metadata. Allow preparation without a forward context by falling back to the input shape.

Expanded dispatch needs an expert backend that consumes grouped rows efficiently. Enabling it for large prefills is deferred to a backend-specific follow-up with rank-coordinated policy, tuning and serving validation. Capacity-based allocations may use more memory than the previous synchronized eager path; this PR claims no general speedup or memory reduction.

Duplicate-work check: open DeepEP PRs were inspected. #51589 proposes opt-in adaptive prefill dispatch; this change makes non-expanded dispatch unconditional. It does not duplicate #50511's padding fix or #59687's SP buffer sizing fix. Future expanded-prefill work should coordinate with #51589.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review and validation. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing every changed line, running relevant tests, and defending the change.

## Test Plan

Exercise prepare/finalize contracts and BF16/FP8 expert outputs across eager execution, capture/replay and return to eager. Validate exact 8k/16k synthetic prefills, full GSM8K, and non-overloaded 8k-input/1k-output serving with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

## Test Result

<details>
<summary>Validation results, reproduction commands and limitations</summary>

Merge resolution `3dab3e92b5` (2026-10-13) merges main `624a5ddafd` and preserves its deferred expert-side routing globalization with unconditional non-expanded dispatch. The existing capture-transition contract now covers both standalone and deferred globalization. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed (including mypy and DCO); `git diff --check` passed. Five CPU contracts passed using the edited implementation with explicit dependency shims, not native DeepEP/CUDA. Native pytest could not load the repository conftest because the local environment lacks `regex`; DeepEP is also unavailable. GPU/model validation has not been rerun on this merge revision; the historical results below retain their stated revision limits.

Cleanup revision `c3726d0063`: independent agent review found no unresolved issues; all applicable pre-commit hooks passed. Four isolated CPU contracts passed against the edited implementation, using dependency shims (not native DeepEP/CUDA). The contract suite is now included alongside the MoE suite in the two-B200 Buildkite job. GPU/model results below were run before the dead-code cleanup and have not been rerun on the final cleanup revision.

GPU validation source `b8b6e0a5d3dad211fece907652ba5cab0cdd8e76`; candidate `80be71926f78838448b2026aa28665df7001e532` applies it to pinned main `d09ff7763747bbe7cd153edd8017479804f47be7`. Run `pr59337-capture-state-20261006-r13` uses model `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-block` revision `6b2399be90eff484848cbbabd684930e01400d54`, image `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:0ad6fa4178c34f4e04402452bbc4294df6dd2fb2785a0ecd402b2861aea2a189`, and report-card `59dcfb2a36827c450eb6ddb1d9d8f7e91e62ae58`. DP2/EP on two B200 GPUs on healthy `b200-02`, fixed 8 GiB KV allocation per GPU. Model context 32768, max batched tokens 16384, max sequences 32, prefix caching disabled.

- All applicable commit-time pre-commit hooks, including mypy and DCO sign-off, passed; Ruff, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Prepare/finalize contracts: **4 passed**; two-GPU MoE suite: **17 passed**, no failures/errors/skips.
- Both synthetic variants completed all 100 measured iterations at 8k and 16k after five warmup iterations. The previously failing 16k case now passes; this does not establish the cause of the old expanded-path timeout.

| ISL per DP rank | PR graphs enabled | PR enforce-eager |
|---|---:|---:|
| 8192 | 110.89 ms | 116.30 ms |
| 16384 | 266.88 ms | 276.34 ms |

Times are coordinated forward completion per exact batch, not HTTP TTFT/TPOT. One fresh process per configuration; no statistical significance claimed. Large received shapes can exceed the normal FlashInfer tuning range and use fallback tactics. The earlier graph-enabled main reference was 111.14/268.21 ms at 8k/16k; it is historical, used a different GPU allocation on the same healthy node, and is not a fresh paired control.

| Synthetic case | Sampled peak GPU A / GPU B (GiB) |
|---|---:|
| Graphs enabled, 8192 | 32.75 / 32.71 |
| Graphs enabled, 16384 | 36.22 / 36.13 |
| Enforce-eager, 8192 | 34.58 / 34.58 |
| Enforce-eager, 16384 | 36.90 / 36.90 |

Full GSM8K: **88.93%**, 1319 questions, five shots, temperature 0, seed 42, max output 256, concurrency 8, zero invalid answers. This passes the configured 85% evaluation threshold. The earlier 89.76% result used a different 2k batched-token budget; this run uses 16k, so it does **not** establish matched accuracy parity.

Serving benchmark: exact 8192-token inputs / 1024-token outputs, four warmup requests then eight measured requests, 0.05 requests/s, concurrency <=2, burstiness 1000, seed 100, ignored EOS. **8 completed, 0 failed**, 65536 input / 8192 output tokens. Mean TTFT **131.69 ms**, TPOT **5.218 ms/token**. Sampled waiting requests and preemption counters were zero. No fresh matched serving baseline or serving speedup claim.

Serving sampled GPU peaks: **32.60 / 32.25 GiB**. Synthetic NVML samples are 100 ms, serving NVML samples one second, restricted to measurement phases. These include allocator reservations, can miss transient allocations, and follow earlier workload steps; no blanket no-worse memory claim. Successful measurement windows were checked for complete GPU/RSS telemetry. The serving process ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` and completed without a checker error.

Commands:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_async_finalize.py -vv -s
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py -vv -s
PYTHONPATH=/work/vllm:/scripts/report-card-worker.pyz \
VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 \
.venv/bin/python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone \
  --nproc-per-node=2 /scripts/rank_driver.py pr1
# Repeat synthetic run with pr-eager and its enforce_eager=True resolved spec.
.venv/bin/python /scripts/gsm8k.py /results/pr59337-capture-state-20261006-r13/serving/pr-graph
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
  --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-block --tokenizer "$PINNED_MODEL_SNAPSHOT" \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 8 \
  --request-rate 0.05 --burstiness 1000 --max-concurrency 2 \
  --seed 100 --save-result --save-detailed --result-dir "$CASE_RESULTS"
```

Full scripts, source hashes, pinned model/image identities, per-rank reports, XML/logs, evaluation outputs, benchmark results and telemetry are retained under `/results/pr59337-capture-state-20261006-r13` on Pirate's `tms-shared-cache` PVC. Local analysis is recorded in `report-card-r13/summarize.py`. The matrix and serving validation completed with Job exit 0; temporary RDMA quota was restored.


Superseded expanded-policy experiments are omitted from this description. Their logs remain under `/results/pr59337-capture-state-20261006-r11` and `...-r12`; they do not validate this revision.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Port Mistral Large 4 AMD indexer cache to get_kv_cache_config
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Mistral Large 4 fails to start on ROCm on `main`: every worker crashes at model init because the AMD `MistralIndexerCache` is still abstract. #61452 replaced `AttentionLayerBase.get_kv_cache_spec` with the abstract `get_kv_cache_config`, and #64534 (Mistral Large 4) merged a day later still implementing only `get_kv_cache_spec`.

## Claims

- Fixes the ROCm startup crash `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MistralIndexerCache without an implementation for abstract method 'get_kv_cache_config'` for Mistral Large 4.
- No behavior change otherwise: the indexer cache spec is identical to before, now wrapped in a `KVCacheLayerConfig` under `FullAttentionManager`, as `DeepseekV32IndexerCache` does.

## Validation

**Regression test:** on ROCm, `test_indexer_k_cache_write` in `tests/models/mistral/test_fused_ops.py` now builds the real `MistralIndexerCache` and checks that the page its `get_kv_cache_config()` requests matches the cache the kernels are tested on. Run on MI300 (gfx942):

<details>
<summary>Without fix</summary>


commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] OCP MX emulation: dequantize only the routed experts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On GPUs without native OCP MX support (e.g. MI250X), MXFP4/MXFP6 MoE layers run through `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts`, which dequantizes every local expert to bf16/fp16 on every forward. A decode batch usually routes to a small fraction of the experts, so this PR dequantizes only the routed ones when they are at most a quarter of the local experts. Related, touching the same class but not this path: #43983 (oracle test coverage), #52868 (`a2_scale` forwarding).

Credit: @ekuznetsov139 had the same idea earlier in #40055 (single-token decode; on MI325 it took Qwen3-235B from about 4 to 21 tok/s). Its capturable single-token path is folded in here (5a4baceea, co-authored by him).

## Claims

- When a batch routes to at most a quarter of the local experts, `apply` gathers the routed experts' packed weights and scales, dequantizes only those, and renumbers `topk_ids` onto the gathered set. For multi-token batches this uses `torch.unique(..., return_inverse=True)`. For a single token (from #40055) it uses a sort of the token's ids and an argsort, so shapes are static and the path also runs under CUDA-graph capture.
- The output is unchanged when both paths select the same Triton tile config: each token is multiplied by the same dequantized expert weights. Tuned config files are keyed by expert count, and the routed path looks up the gathered count, so on a GPU with a tuned file for the full shape the full path may use a tuned tile while the routed path uses the default one, and the outputs can then differ by rounding. vLLM has no tuned configs for MI250X, so both paths use the default config there; the test checks bit-identity with `torch.equal`.
- Past a quarter, for an empty batch, for multi-token batches under CUDA-graph capture, and with an `expert_map` (EP), LoRA experts or w1/w2 biases, the existing full dequantization runs unchanged.
- One MoE layer of a 256-expert MXFP4 model at TP8 on MI250X: 6.6 ms per call before, 1.5 ms with 8 routed experts (c=1), 2.3 ms with 31 (c=4). This is a microbenchmark; see Validation.

## Validation

**Microbenchmark, MI250X (gfx90a), one MoE layer** of a large 256-expert MXFP4 MoE model at TP8, measured on a GCD that was busy with other work (the routed rows include the gather):

| routed experts | time per call |
|---|---|
| all (main) | 6.6 ms |
| 8 (c=1 decode) | 1.5 ms |
| 31 (c=4) | 2.3 ms |
| 100 (gather forced) | 6.2 ms |
| 225 (gather forced) | 15.5 ms |

The last two rows were measured with the gather forced, to pick the threshold. With 256 experts the threshold is 64, so this PR sends both to the full path. The layer output was bit-identical in every row (default tile configs on both paths).

**No end-to-end number.** This change has not been served end to end on this base. Before the change, c=1 decode of that model (TP8 x PP3) ran at about 2.4 tok/s.

**Test**, `test_emulation_routed_dequant_moe_forward_is_bit_identical` in `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py` (ROCm only, using that file's `ROCM_AVAILABLE` skip): a real MXFP4 emulation MoE forward with 32 experts. A spy on `_dequantize_weights` records how many experts each call dequantizes; the test runs once normally, once with the capture flag patched on (only the single-token case stays routed), and once with the full path forced, and compares outputs with `torch.equal`. Three cases: 4 tokens routed to 5 experts (routed path), 5 tokens routed to 9 experts, past the threshold of 8 (full path), and 1 token routed to 2 experts (single-token path).

<details>
<summary>commands and output (1x MI250X, gfx90a, main 8e2beaa3b)</summary>

```
$ pytest kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k test_emulation_routed_dequant_moe_forward_is_bit_identical     # with this change
3 passed, 181 deselected in 44.74s

# without (non-test files reverted to main)
E       AssertionError: assert [32, 32] == [5, 5]
E       AttributeError: <class '...OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts'> has no attribute '_routed_experts'
E       AssertionError: assert [32, 32] == [2, 2]
3 failed, 181 deselected in 9.72s
# (the past-threshold case fails on main only because the test patches the new helper)

# real CUDA-graph capture of one token through apply(), replayed with other expert ids
dequant sizes during capture: [2, 2]
replay ids=[30, 2]: equal_to_full_dequant=True maxdiff=0
replay ids=[5, 17]: equal_to_full_dequant=True maxdiff=0
replay ids=[0, 31]: equal_to_full_dequant=True maxdiff=0
replay ids=[9, 9]: equal_to_full_dequant=True maxdiff=0
replay ids=[12, 3]: equal_to_full_dequant=True maxdiff=0
```

Rebased on main `db3b0f0fa`: ruff, typos, SPDX and mypy (3.11 hook) are clean (ruff re-run after the fold-in). The test is skipped on CPU and CUDA hosts.
</details>

**Not tested:** MXFP6 schemes (same code path; only the dequantization function differs); end-to-end throughput.

## Details

**Host sync.** Outside graph capture, multi-token batches add one `torch.unique` per MoE layer per forward, which synchronizes with the host. It runs before the threshold check, so batches that end up on the full path pay it too. Under capture, multi-token batches take the full path, as they do today. The single-token path (from #40055) has no host sync and a fixed size (`topk` slots), so batch-1 decode graphs capture it; a repeated id there would only cost a duplicate gather.

**Threshold.** A quarter of the local experts is where, on MI250X, the gather and renumbering cost about as much as the dequantization they save (the 100-expert row above is already at parity with the full path). It is a constant in `apply`, not a config knob.

**Why not EP/LoRA/bias.** With an `expert_map` the ids are global and would need remapping before the gather; LoRA and biases index per-expert tensors that the gather does not cover. These cases keep the full path rather than growing this change.
AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Quantization][Perf] Fuse the block Hadamard input rotation into AITER's MXFP4 activation quant
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, `mxfp4_hadamard32` layers on AITER's ASM MXFP4 GEMM now rotate their input inside the activation quant ([ROCm/aiter#6734](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6734)) instead of in a separate PyTorch kernel, which recovers the 6–12% serving throughput that #62750's rotation costs on Qwen3.8-2.4T.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for "hadamard mxfp4" and "hadamard rotation aiter"; #65398 adds a MoE variant of the online scheme and does not fuse the rotation.

## Claims

- TP8 serving output throughput is within 0.6% of plain RTN `mxfp4` at concurrency 4, 64 and 256. With #62750's PyTorch rotation it is 6.0–12.4% lower.
- Per layer, the fused rotation adds 0–5% to quant + GEMM, where the PyTorch rotation adds 70–170%.
- The output matches the PyTorch rotation up to bf16 rounding, so #62750's accuracy results carry over.

## Validation

8x MI355X, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B Quark MXFP4, TP8. vLLM nightly `df3bd094` plus the arm's diff, with ROCm/aiter#6734 ported to its AITER 0.1.25. All arms put the GDN projections (`in_proj_qkvz`, `out_proj`) and the shared experts on online MXFP4 (322 layers) and differ only in the GDN projections' scheme.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1 AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --load-format dummy \
  --compilation-config '{"splitting_ops": [], "pass_config": {"fuse_rope_kvcache": true, "enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion": true, "fuse_allreduce_rms": true}}' \
  --quantization-config.targets '{"*shared_expert*": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.in_proj_qkv": "mxfp4_hadamard32", "*linear_attn.in_proj_z": "mxfp4_hadamard32", "*linear_attn.out_proj": "mxfp4_hadamard32"}'

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --ignore-eos --max-concurrency {4,64,256} --num-prompts {32,256,1024} --seed {1,2}
```

The RTN arm uses `"mxfp4"` for the three GDN targets.

**Serving**, mean of 2 repeats (repeats differ by up to 1.6%), fresh caches per arm:

| GDN projections | Output tok/s c=4 | c=64 | c=256 | Mean TPOT ms c=4 | c=64 | c=256 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RTN `mxfp4` | 373.0 | 1807.1 | 4028.3 | 10.45 | 34.09 | 60.91 |
| `mxfp4_hadamard32`, PyTorch rotation (#62750) | 326.9 (-12.4%) | 1694.4 (-6.2%) | 3787.7 (-6.0%) | 11.94 | 36.23 | 64.86 |
| `mxfp4_hadamard32`, fused (this PR) | 371.3 (-0.5%) | 1796.6 (-0.6%) | 4024.2 (-0.1%) | 10.50 | 34.21 | 61.09 |

**Per layer**, quant + GEMM in µs, one GPU, CUDA graph:

| M | `in_proj_qkvz` plain | PyTorch rotation | Fused | `out_proj` plain | PyTorch rotation | Fused |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 7.2 | 15.3 | 7.4 | 5.3 | 10.9 | 5.0 |
| 16 | 9.5 | 17.1 | 9.2 | 5.4 | 12.6 | 5.6 |
| 256 | 14.7 | 28.1 | 15.0 | 8.0 | 17.6 | 8.5 |
| 1024 | 29.3 | 65.1 | 29.6 | 16.9 | 32.5 | 17.0 |
| 8192 | 170.6 | 459.1 | 175.7 | 83.5 | 155.5 | 88.0 |

**Accuracy.** On the same inputs, the fused and PyTorch rotations give the same relative error against the unquantized GEMM to five digits at every M from 1024 to 16384. Up to 0.07% of output elements differ (fp32 butterfly vs bf16 matmul, then the same bf16 rounding before FP4). #62750 measured this rotation on Qwen3.8-2.4T with real weights (thinking on, paired seeds, exact McNemar):

| Eval | BF16 → `mxfp4_hadamard32` | Fixed / broken | p | Length vs BF16 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K, 12 reps | 96.34 → 96.13 | +125 / -158 | 0.057 | 1.026 [1.000, 1.052] |
| GPQA Diamond, 5 reps | 92.3 → 93.1 | +20 / -12 | 0.22 | 0.940 [0.904, 0.977] |

**Unit tests** (MI355X, stock nightly `be47189f` with AITER 0.1.29), 91 passed, 4 skipped, with and without `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`:

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_input_hadamard.py tests/quantization/test_online_mxfp4.py \
  tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py tests/v1/determinism/test_mx_linear_batch_invariant.py
```

`test_input_hadamard.py` fails if the ASM path stops fusing, if the Triton or emulation path starts, or if the wrapper rotates twice. `test_online_mxfp4.py` fails if the fake `gemm_with_dynamic_quant` drifts from the op again.

## Details

- `InputHadamardFusable` (in `input_hadamard.py`) is an opt-in mixin with `fuse_input_hadamard(layer, size) -> bool`. `InputHadamardLinearMethod` still rotates the weight, and skips its input rotation when the wrapped method is fusable and returns `True`. Online MXFP4, `QuarkLinearMethod` and Quark OCP MX inherit it and forward the call to their `MxFp4LinearKernel`.
- `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel` fuses only on its ASM GEMM path with size 32, and passes `hadamard_rotate=True` to the HIP quant. The Triton path keeps the PyTorch rotation. The server logs `... rotates its input by the 32-wide Hadamard matrix itself.` once per method.
- The ASM path is used only for (N, K) in AITER's tuned a4w4 config. `out_proj` is tuned today; ROCm/aiter#7441 adds the `in_proj_qkvz` (N=4608, K=8192) config that the numbers above include.
- Also fixes the fake impl of `gemm_with_dynamic_quant`, whose signature had drifted from the op.

**Limitations and CI gaps.** Serving used dummy weights, and accuracy was measured on #62750's unfused path; the fused path's equivalence rests on the per-element comparison above. No CI job runs these tests until the Quantization jobs are re-enabled (#66900, #66672). The MI355 job will then cover the fused path: the AITER cases turn AITER on themselves, since CI does not set `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER`.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Prevent NVSHMEM IB transport setup hang in DBO GSM8K tests
commits.pr_body:
#### Overview
Fixes the intermittent NVSHMEM startup hang in `test_dbo_v2_features_gsm8k` on single-node multi-GPU runs (fixes part of #67307).

#### Root Cause
When the two GPUs sit on different CPU NUMA sockets, NVSHMEM and DeepEP attempt to initialize InfiniBand Queue Pairs across host NICs (`ibv_modify_qp failed`), causing the background test server to hang indefinitely until the CI timeout.

#### Fix
Pass `NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none` and `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST=none` to `RemoteOpenAIServer` in `tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py`. This keeps NVSHMEM strictly on the local NVLink fabric and off host NICs for single-node execution, following the identical pattern merged in #61695 and #66207.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Correct the batch-invariance comment on Hopper/Blackwell split-k
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The comment in `enable_batch_invariant_mode` for SM90/SM100 says that split-k is the only source of batch variance on those GPUs and that the cuBLAS workspace config disables it. That is not accurate for every shape: with split-k disabled, some narrow shapes such as MoE router projections are still not batch invariant in cuBLAS, which is why #35404 routes unquantized Linear layers to the Triton `linear_batch_invariant` on every CUDA device. The comment as written suggests cuBLAS is enough on Hopper/Blackwell (it led me to propose the opposite in #65569). This changes the comment only; no code changes.

## Evidence

From the discussion in #65569 (raw data linked there): under batch-invariant mode's settings, the gpt-oss-20b router (32 x 2880) differs between a row computed alone and inside a batch on H100 and H200, and on H100 narrow widths (N <= 96 at K = 2880/4096/5120, and widths 97-127 that are not multiples of 8) also differ, while wide projections pass.

## Test Plan

Comment-only change.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Fail pulls from a lost prefill worker
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When a prefill worker dies, the Mooncake decoder does not notice. Its pull waits up to `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT + 60` = 540 s for P's reply while holding the request's KV blocks, because ZMQ reconnects silently instead of reporting the lost peer. D also keeps the dead worker's address cached, so the requests queued behind send their pulls there and wait another 540 s. Under load, D's KV stays full of requests that can never finish.

This PR fails a pull as soon as its connection is lost, and makes D look P up again. It is the decoder-side counterpart of #64193.

## Claims

- **P process dies:** the requests waiting on it fail within 2–4 s, instead of after 545 s plus a second 540 s wave.
- **P frozen or unreachable:** they fail once heartbeats or the existing timeouts expire, all within 102 s.
- No change for a live P and no new option. Failures follow `kv_load_failure_policy`.

## Validation

**Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake*.py` → 750 passed, 5 skipped. 4 more cases hit Hugging Face Hub fetch errors and pass on rerun.
- The new test runs a ZMQ ROUTER in a subprocess that takes the pull and never answers. The ROUTER is then killed, frozen with `SIGSTOP`, or never listening. All three cases time out on main and pass in about 1 s with this PR.
- This PR also fixes `test_mooncake_stats.py::test_expired_request_bumps_counter`, which has been broken since #64193.

`pre-commit` passes.

**End to end:**
- Setup: 2× A800, DeepSeek-MoE-16B, TP=1 per side, `kv_lease_duration=30`.
- Load: 128 requests at 2.4× D's KV capacity.
- Failure: P's process group gets the signal at t≈41 s. Times are measured from the signal.

| | main, `SIGKILL` | this PR, `SIGKILL` | this PR, `SIGSTOP` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stranded requests fail | 545 s, then 1,084 s | 2–4 s | 12–102 s |
| D's KV usage below 50% | 556 s | 5.5 s | 109 s |
| Requests ok / failed | 53 / 75 | 54 / 74 | 53 / 75 |

## Details

**Root cause**
1. D allocates blocks for a request, sends a pull to P's ZMQ ROUTER, and waits for the reply.
2. If P dies, D's DEALER silently reconnects, or keeps retrying a refused connect, so the wait runs to the 540 s timeout. The reply can never arrive: the DEALER has no routing id, so P's ROUTER drops replies addressed to a lost connection.
3. `_remote_agents` is never invalidated, so later requests pull from the same dead address.

**Fix**
- D monitors each pull socket for `EVENT_DISCONNECTED | EVENT_CONNECT_RETRIED`. On either event, it fails the pull through `_handle_failed_recv`, and drops the cached addresses of every engine that lists this worker. Later requests then query the bootstrap server again: a dead P fails at once, and a restarted P is found.
- ZMTP heartbeats (2 s / 10 s, as in `kv_offload/tiering/p2p/control/zmq.py`) make a frozen or unreachable P drop the connection too. libzmq applies them only when they are set before `connect()`, so `make_zmq_socket` takes them as arguments.

**Tradeoffs and limitations**
- A pull whose connect hits a transient network error now fails, where ZMQ would have retried it.
- Frozen P: pulls sent before D notices wait for ZMQ's 30 s handshake timeout. Requests queued after that wait for the bootstrap query to time out (3 × `VLLM_MOONCAKE_CONNECTOR_TIMEOUT`), hence the 102 s.
- Cost: one inproc monitor socket per pull, about 30 µs.

#35943 and #37745 reported this hang and were closed as not planned. No open PR covers it.

**AI assistance:** written with Claude Code. I reviewed every changed line, ran all tests and experiments above, and can answer for the design.

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Set the CPU tier up in the background under async_init
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Milestone 1 of #66570. Builds on #66391; only the last two commits are new.

With `"async_init": true`, workers map the CPU region and return right away. A background thread then pre-faults and pins it, while the engine serves without offloading. Offloading turns on once every worker reports ready.

- The setup thread switches itself to relaxed capture mode, so pinning can't invalidate a CUDA graph capture. That race is what reverted #45850. If the mode can't be set, setup fails and offloading stays off.
- It pins one small call at a time (a worker slot, or whole rows up to 8 MiB) and sleeps `async_init_pin_pace` (default 2.0) times each call's duration after it. Back-to-back registrations hold a driver lock and stall serving.
- Readiness goes through the connector's existing worker metadata, so nothing outside the offloading connector changes. Once #62337 lands, this gate moves to the core.
- If setup fails, offloading stays off and the engine keeps serving.
- CUDA only; other platforms set up synchronously. Off by default.

This covers `CPUOffloadingSpec`. `TieringOffloadingSpec` ignores the option with a warning until the follow-up. #54578 proposes the same key with a different design; the two need to be reconciled.

## Results

Startup to `/health` OK, with the Tiering follow-up on top:

| Setup | Sync | async_init |
|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3, 16 H100 (4 pods), 280 GiB/rank | 439 s | 334 s |
| Qwen3-8B (dummy weights), TP=4, 1,250 GiB | 241.5 s | 57-61 s |

On GLM, pre-fault (117 s) and pinning (12 s) leave the critical path. That run used an earlier build without pacing; pinning started after healthy, so the healthy time is the same.

Request latency while pinning runs (Qwen3-8B, 1,250 GiB, one 9 MiB slot per call):

| Pinning | Worst latency | Time to pin |
|---|---|---|
| Unpaced (3 runs) | 0.4-1.4 s | 23 s |
| Paced 2x | 0.18 s | 51-55 s |

Latency before pinning started was 0.084 s.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
```

Plus, on 2x H100 80GB at this head: a standalone capture race, and `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --tensor-parallel-size 2` with an 8 GiB CPU tier and a GPU cache small enough to evict.

## Test Result

Unit suites on H100, against #66391 at `b052cf92f3`:

- `tests/v1/kv_offload`: 1017 passed, 6 skipped (1011 before).
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector`: 742 passed (740 before).

Capture race, 200 global-mode graph captures while a second thread calls `cudaHostRegister`:

| Second thread | Captures failed |
|---|---|
| default capture mode | 200 / 200 (`cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated`) |
| relaxed, as the setup thread does | 0 / 200 across 199,103 registrations |

End to end (Qwen3-0.6B, TP=2, 8 GiB tier):

- Sync and `async_init` stored the same 4.07 GB, loaded the same 360 MB back from CPU for an evicted prompt (3,136 of 3,162 tokens cached) and returned the same text.
- With `async_init_pin_pace=30`, pinning took 16-18 s per rank and overlapped the second graph-capture pass; both passes completed. Offloading turned on 11 s into a 22 s request; the chunks it skipped were stored afterwards (462 MB) and loaded back after eviction.
- Injected failure: with the capture-mode switch removed, `cudaHostRegister` fails during warmup and the engine does not come up.
- `TieringOffloadingSpec` with `async_init` logs the warning, sets up synchronously and serves the same results.

The 8 GiB tier is too small to show the startup gain; the Results above cover that.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][Perf] Add H100 BF16 batch-invariant matmul configs for gpt-oss
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Related to #65569 and the batch-invariance performance tracker #27433. Add Hopper BF16 persistent-matmul configs, in the format of #62219, for the bf16 Linear shapes that popular models send through `linear_batch_invariant` under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4.1, gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b. In GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1 everything else is FP8/FP4 and uses other kernels, so the bf16 layers are the routers, the sparse-attention indexer projections, DeepSeek-V4.1's compressor and `lm_head` (per rank at TP=8 and TP=4). gpt-oss-20b's and gpt-oss-120b's unquantized attention, routers and `lm_head` run this kernel since #35404. The Triton path is unchanged; nothing is routed to cuBLAS.

## Claims

- Invariance: each shape uses one `BLOCK_K` across all M buckets. A row multiplied alone vs. inside batches of M = 1..1024 and every 16th M up to 8192 (first 8, last 8 and 4 middle rows): 0 of 438,030 rows differ over all 15 shapes.
- Kernel speed on H100: the tuned configs are 1.08x-3.04x faster than the default config at every bucket of every shape (table below).
- End to end on one H100 (`vllm bench serve`, 3 alternating rounds, raw logs in the comments below): gpt-oss-20b: decode-heavy output throughput +4.3% over main (faster in 3 of 3 rounds; loss against batch invariance off 22.8% -> 19.5%), prefill-heavy request throughput +2.4% (faster in 2 of 3 rounds); gpt-oss-120b: decode-heavy output throughput +1.9% over main (faster in 3 of 3 rounds; loss against batch invariance off 22.1% -> 20.6%), prefill-heavy request throughput +0.9% (faster in 2 of 3 rounds). The gains are modest because gpt-oss's MoE experts use another kernel; the same will hold for GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1, where only the layers above are bf16.
- New test `test_hopper_tuned_linear_batch_invariance` checks config selection and exact first/last-row equality on both sides of every bucket boundary for all 15 shapes. `tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py` on H100: 50 passed (15 new cases).

## Shapes and kernel times

Speedup over the default config / time relative to cuBLAS, at M = 1, 32, 256, 2048:

| Model | Layer | (N, K) | BLOCK_K | M=1 | M=32 | M=256 | M=2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3 | MoE router | (256, 6144) | 128 | 2.53x / 1.84 | 2.57x / 1.66 | 2.59x / 1.38 | 1.99x / 1.14 |
| GLM-5.3 | indexer `wk_weights_proj` | (160, 6144) | 128 | 2.51x / 1.95 | 2.59x / 1.72 | 2.55x / 1.61 | 2.08x / 1.08 |
| GLM-5.3 | `lm_head`, TP=8 | (19360, 6144) | 64 | 2.57x / 1.02 | 2.21x / 1.02 | 1.27x / 1.26 | 1.44x / 0.98 |
| GLM-5.3 | `lm_head`, TP=4 | (38720, 6144) | 64 | 2.12x / 1.00 | 1.86x / 1.03 | 1.26x / 1.13 | 1.30x / 1.17 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | MoE router | (384, 5120) | 128 | 2.48x / 1.56 | 2.50x / 1.41 | 2.33x / 1.37 | 1.72x / 1.23 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | indexer `weights_proj` | (32, 5120) | 128 | 2.37x / 1.78 | 2.37x / 1.57 | 2.38x / 1.47 | 2.54x / 1.09 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | indexer `wk` | (128, 512) | 128 | 1.41x / 1.03 | 1.45x / 0.98 | 1.48x / 0.97 | 1.32x / 0.98 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | compressor `fused_wkv_wgate` | (1024, 5120) | 128 | 2.57x / 1.42 | 2.57x / 1.28 | 2.38x / 1.12 | 1.20x / 1.21 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | `lm_head`, TP=8 | (16160, 5120) | 64 | 2.51x / 0.95 | 2.20x / 0.96 | 1.34x / 1.05 | 1.41x / 1.08 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | `lm_head`, TP=4 | (32320, 5120) | 64 | 2.33x / 0.96 | 2.02x / 0.97 | 1.38x / 1.02 | 1.37x / 0.99 |
| gpt-oss-20b | qkv_proj | (5120, 2880) | 128 | 2.83x / 1.06 | 2.47x / 1.07 | 1.13x / 1.37 | 1.14x / 1.29 |
| gpt-oss-20b | o_proj | (2880, 4096) | 128 | 3.04x / 1.09 | 2.57x / 1.05 | 1.64x / 1.21 | 1.08x / 1.50 |
| gpt-oss-20b | `lm_head` | (201088, 2880) | 64 | 2.56x / 0.96 | 2.07x / 0.98 | 1.41x / 1.04 | 1.26x / 1.03 |
| gpt-oss-20b | MoE router | (32, 2880) | 128 | 2.13x / 1.27 | 2.07x / 1.19 | 2.08x / 1.17 | 2.51x / 0.99 |
| gpt-oss-120b | MoE router | (128, 2880) | 128 | 2.12x / 1.30 | 2.14x / 1.16 | 2.06x / 1.14 | 1.89x / 1.13 |

Shapes were read from the GLM-5.3 checkpoint and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's safetensors headers and matched to vLLM's model code (`GateLinear` falls back to `ReplicatedLinear` under batch invariance; the indexer and compressor projections are unquantized; `lm_head` is vocab-parallel).

## Validation

H100 80GB HBM3 (SXM), torch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, vLLM nightly 0.33.0rc1.dev454 with this diff applied. Tuning: for each shape and `BLOCK_K` in {64, 128}, the fastest (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, num_warps, num_stages) per bucket, timed at the bucket's largest M; the `BLOCK_K` kept has the lowest mean log time ratio to cuBLAS.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py -k hopper_tuned
```

Serving (gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b): fresh `vllm serve` per run, `--max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --max-concurrency 32 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 20261105 --num-warmups 20`, 2,000 prompts per run; decode-heavy 512 in / 256 out, prefill-heavy 1,024 in / 4 out; main and patch alternate which goes first, batch invariance off measured in every round.

## Not yet measured

End-to-end runs of GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1 need a full 8-GPU H200/H100 node, which takes days to get on our cluster; in progress. H200 uses the same `hopper` table but was not benchmarked.

Tuning script and raw outputs: https://github.com/imthomp/vllm-batch-invariance (`src/tune_bi.py`, `results/tune`, `results/serve_gptoss`, `results/serve_gptoss120b`).

commits.pr_title: [Config] Make --monokernel and decode_backend=latency_specialized one switch
commits.pr_body:
Human written Summary:

While reviewing this https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66184, which is to use `--monokernal` config to replace the legacy mono-kernel enablement code for MiniMax-M31 ( I did it during Day 0 time which is the early stage of mono-kernel era in vLLM ) using the environment variable, I knew we also have a different way of enabling it. For example, when I enabled the mono kernel for the Mistral-large-4  (PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64534), I used `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}` . so, to make things easier, I put up this PR to let these two config options alias each other .  

## Purpose

Two switches turn on a model's specialized decode (RFC #60904), and each model reads only one:


| Switch | Read by (main) |
| --- | --- |
| `--monokernel` (`KernelConfig.monokernel`) | DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 AMD, Muse Spark AMD, MiniMax-M3 AMD |
| `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'` | DeepSeek-V4.1, GLM5next, Kimi-K3, Muse Spark (NVIDIA); Kimi-K3 AMD; MiniMax-M3.1 NVIDIA (#66324) |
| Both, through a per-model alias | Mistral Large 4 AMD (#64534): its `decode_backend()` returns `latency_specialized` when `kernel_config.monokernel` is set |

Except where a model adds its own alias, as Mistral Large 4 does, the other switch is silently ignored. `additional_config` is not validated, so passing `decode_backend` to an AMD model that reads `--monokernel`, or the reverse, starts the stock decode with no error or log. Recipes that serve one model on both vendors have to pass both switches (Muse Spark already does). MiniMax-M3.1 will have the same split once #66324 (NVIDIA, `decode_backend`) and #66184 (AMD, `--monokernel`) land.

This PR makes them one switch in `VllmConfig.__post_init__`:

- `decode_backend=latency_specialized` sets `kernel_config.monokernel=True`.
- `--monokernel` sets `additional_config["decode_backend"]="latency_specialized"`.
- `--monokernel` with any other `decode_backend` value (e.g. `auto`) is an error.
- Both spellings give the same compile factors, so they share the compile cache.

No model reads both switches with different meanings: each model and vendor directory reads only one, and the CUDA-only hooks in common files are gated on `current_platform.is_cuda()`. The alias therefore only turns on what the user asked for, on the model's own path. A `SupportsCompileFactors` (non-dict) `additional_config` is left unchanged.

Also: the Muse Spark AMD DSpark draft warned "specialized decode is not supported on ROCm" whenever `decode_backend` was set. On AMD that switch now enables the target's monokernel, so the message becomes an info line saying that only the draft keeps its stock layers.

## Not a duplicate

`gh pr list --state open` searches for "monokernel decode_backend", "monokernel alias" and "latency_specialized alias" find model PRs that each use one switch (#61662, #65566, #60889, #65985, #66324, #61568) and a docs PR (#62256) that documents both. None of them unify the two. RFC #60904's text names `decode_backend`, and its comments treat both switches as valid.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/test_config.py -k "monokernel or decode_backend or neither_switch"`: three new tests. Either spelling sets both switches and hashes the same, the default sets neither, and a conflicting `decode_backend` raises.

## Test Result



- With the change: 5 passed. Without it (`vllm/config/vllm.py` reverted): 4 failed, 1 passed (the default case).
- Run against this branch's Python on a ROCm nightly image (`2b009fc`), with the tests in a standalone file. The full `tests/test_config.py` does not collect on that image: its compiled ops are older than main (`torch.ops._C.rotary_embedding` is missing). CI covers the full file.
- Muse Spark ROCm: `import vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.dspark` works; `pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` (CPU tests): 16 passed. The 26 gfx950 tiny-model tests were not run (GPUs busy); they do not cover the changed lines. No Muse Spark serve run (TP8, 816B).
- Muse Spark serve on MI350X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (`153dc0464`, 2026-11-13) with this PR's `vllm/` diff applied, the recipe's AMD MXFP4 command (`amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8 + EP, 7-token DSpark, AITER FA, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`), and one chat request ("What is 17 * 23?"):

  | Image | Switch | "Muse Spark monokernel attached" | Draft warning | Answer |
  | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
  | nightly + this PR | `--monokernel` | 8 / 8 ranks | once | `391` |
  | nightly + this PR | `decode_backend=latency_specialized` only | 8 / 8 ranks | once | `391` |
  | nightly (main) | `decode_backend=latency_specialized` only | **0 / 8 ranks** | once | `391` |

  On main, `decode_backend` is silently ignored by the Muse Spark AMD target; with this PR it starts the same monokernel as `--monokernel`. These runs used the earlier warning wording; the final commit changes only the text. The hipBLASLt `HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR` warnings in the logs (m 8192, n 304-320, k 40960) appear on the unpatched nightly too.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.
- No serving change for existing commands: a deployment that passed one switch keeps the same model path. The only new behavior is that the other spelling now works too.

## Notes

AI assistance was used for this change. I reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Select only batch-invariant MXFP8 linear kernels under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the MXFP8 linear kernel selector on CUDA could pick Marlin or FlashInfer, whose output for a row changes with the batch size. This PR gives the MXFP8 linear kernels a `supports_batch_invariance()` capability and, in batch-invariant mode, drops kernels without it before selection. Related: #27433, #65560 (coverage gap "Batch-invariant execution").

## Claims

- With the flag on, MXFP8 linear layers on CUDA only run on kernels that declare batch invariance: Emulation (default), and Humming (`--linear-backend humming`, and still the default on Hopper). A `--linear-backend` that names another kernel falls back to automatic selection with the existing warning.
- This fixes the default configuration on Ampere/Ada (Marlin) and Blackwell (FlashInfer CuTe-DSL), and `--linear-backend marlin` on any GPU.
- No change with the flag off, on ROCm/XPU, or on the MXFP8 BMM path.

## Test

B200 (SM100), main `919d45fc3a` vs this PR `18b921b1ba` (its parent is that main commit), `flashinfer` 0.7.3, `humming-kernels` 0.1.19. Not rerun on H100 or Ampere/Ada for this revision.
