commits.pr_title: [Recipe][ROCm] ripple-65b on mi350x and mi355x
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This builds on #66721, which added the AMD section of the Ripple-65B-Preview recipe and marked MI355X verified. On top of it, this PR:

- Marks the BF16 variant verified on MI350X too.
- Adds an AMD override that selects `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, in both the rendered command and the guide's `docker run` example. Without the override, ROCm auto-selects `ROCM_ATTN`, which handles DFlash2 verify steps poorly (in terms of throughput performance): 3x slower on GSM8K and 8.7x slower on SPEED-Bench.
- Caps `--max-model-len` at 1048576 on AMD with or without DFlash2. #66721 capped it only with DFlash2, but the KV cache for the full 2,097,152-token context does not fit on one MI350X with either attention backend.

## Claims

- On 1x MI350X, the recipe's AMD command with DFlash2 (`num_speculative_tokens: 7`) matches published accuracy:
  - GSM8K: 0.9424 (strict).
  - GPQA-Diamond: 83.6 ± 2.3, against 85.2 published. 17 of 792 responses ran out of the 65,536-token context before answering; excluding them gives 85.4.
- Throughput: SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k` reaches 470.9 output tok/s at concurrency 16.
- `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` is 3.0x faster than `ROCM_ATTN` on GSM8K and 8.7x faster on SPEED-Bench, with the same accuracy and acceptance length.
- The B300 command does not change.

## Validation

**Setup.** 1x MI350X (gfx950), TP1, BF16.

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model | `ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview` at rev `e27e1717` |
| Drafter | `ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-DFlash2` at rev `35609b3b`, 7 tokens |
| Image | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly@sha256:6eeac5c6`: vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev142+g96710245e`, AITER `0.1.28.post1`, plus the one-line clamp from ROCm/aiter#7539 |

**Recipe.** `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir recipes` passes at vllm-project/recipes@0eb50b4. On AMD, the recipe resolves to the BF16 variant, because NVFP4 is restricted to Blackwell and Rubin. The renderer emits `--max-model-len 1048576` once on MI350X and MI355X, with and without spec decoding.

**Serve command.** This is the recipe's AMD command with reasoning, tool calling and spec decoding on. The last three flags are not part of the recipe and were added for the benchmarks.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --reasoning-parser ripple \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser ripple \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --max-model-len 65536 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
```

**Accuracy and throughput:**

| Benchmark | Settings | Result | Wall time | Acceptance length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K | lm-eval 0.4.13, 5-shot, 1319 samples, `local-completions`, concurrency 64, `max_gen_toks` 2048 | 0.9424 strict / 0.9416 flexible (± 0.0064) | 188.4 s | 5.81 |
| GPQA-Diamond | temperature 0.7, top_p 0.99, `reasoning_effort` max, 4 epochs, 64 parallel tasks | 83.6 ± 2.3 over 792/792 samples, 0 errors | 1 h 54 min | 4.74 |
| SPEED-Bench | `throughput_8k`, `low_entropy` category, 1024 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, concurrency 16, 256 prompts + 16 warmups | 470.9 output tok/s; median TTFT 1181 ms, median TPOT 32.5 ms | 557 s | 3.31 |

During GPQA, generation throughput averaged 1,060 tok/s at 64 running requests. All 256 SPEED-Bench requests completed, with exactly 1024 output tokens each.

**Attention backends.** After merging main (including #66721), I rebuilt the image from this branch with `docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl` (`vllm-openai` target, gfx950): vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev263+g7b723d043` (same tree as 481ca99fc4, before a sign-off amend), AITER `0.1.29`, plus the ROCm/aiter#7539 clamp. Both runs use the recipe's AMD command as rendered, with DFlash2 (7 tokens) and `--max-model-len 1048576`, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. Only `--attention-backend` differs. Benchmark settings match the table above.

| Backend | GSM8K strict / flexible | GSM8K wall time | GSM8K acceptance | SPEED-Bench output tok/s | Median TTFT | Median TPOT | SPEED-Bench acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` | 0.9439 / 0.9431 | 188.5 s | 5.80 | 471.2 | 1182 ms | 32.3 ms | 3.32 |
| `ROCM_ATTN` (auto-selected default) | 0.9416 / 0.9409 | 560.5 s | 5.79 | 54.3 | 15272 ms | 284.4 ms | 3.29 |

Acceptance length is the same for both backends, so the gap is attention time, not drafting. The unified-attention results on the rebuilt image match the nightly results above.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
# GSM8K
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048

# GPQA-Diamond
beam-verifier eval gpqa-diamond --base-url http://localhost:8000/v1 \
  --model-name ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview --parallel-tasks 64 --harness-kwargs epochs=4

# SPEED-Bench (data from NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills speed-bench/prepare.py, throughput_8k config)
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview \
  --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path <prepared dir> \
  --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_8k --speed-bench-category low_entropy \
  --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 256 --num-warmups 16 --max-concurrency 16 --seed 0

# Image used for the attention-backend comparison (run from an export of this branch's HEAD)
STACK_IMAGE=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:base-nightly RUNTIME=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:base-nightly \
  TAG=vllm-rocm:ripple-main docker buildx bake -f docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl vllm-openai \
  --set vllm-openai.args.ARCH=gfx950
```

</details>

## Details

**Why the override is needed.** `_get_backend_priorities` in `vllm/platforms/rocm.py` lists `ROCM_ATTN` first on gfx950, so it is auto-selected for Ripple. Two parts of its `chunked_prefill_paged_decode` path cost speculative decoding:

- Any query longer than one token goes to the Triton `context_attention_fwd` prefix-prefill kernel. Every DFlash2 verify step is a multi-token query, so each step runs a prefill over the full context.
- The ROCm custom paged-attention kernel is turned off on sliding-window layers, which are 64 of Ripple's 80 layers.

`ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` treats spec-decode queries as decode.

#61433 would rank unified attention above `ROCM_ATTN` when spec decoding is on. It is still open, and it would not cover runs without spec decoding.

**Context length.** The guide from #66721 said the full 2,097,152-token context fits without DFlash2. On one MI350X it does not, with either attention backend, so the AMD override now caps `--max-model-len` at 1048576 in both cases. With DFlash2 and unified attention, a needle-retrieval check found the needle at up to 1,022,250 prompt tokens.

Known limitations, not addressed here:

- **GPU memory fault without ROCm/aiter#7539.** With the stock AITER, earlier long GPQA runs with `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` hit `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` after minutes of 64-way spec-decode load. This matches the gfx950 unified-attention block-table prefetch overread that ROCm/aiter#7539 fixes. All runs above use that fix and had no faults. Until it reaches vLLM's AITER pin, long high-concurrency spec-decode runs on gfx950 can still fault.
- **MI355X without DFlash2.** The 1M cap also applies to MI355X, because recipe-level overrides are per brand, not per GPU. MI355X has the same 288 GB of HBM, so it likely hits the same limit, but I did not test it there.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix ROCM_AITER_FA context loss on out-of-order batches
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
A batch can contain a fresh prompt before a request that has cached KV. If the splitter assumes that the first fresh prompt starts the trailing prefill region, it can put the later continuation on a path that ignores its history. The fix changes how the regions are chosen, adds a guard for an all-decode batch whose `max_query_len` is overstated, and sizes the cached-context chunks correctly.
 This PR takes the order-independent split from #63542 (credit @qli88) and adds an all-decode guard for an over-stated `max_query_len`.

## Claims

- Phi-4-mini `niah_single_2` at 30k, 16 concurrent requests: **0.626 → 1.000** on 1× MI300X. Main misses 187 of 500 needles. The earlier three-model run on the same recipe was Phi 0.62 → 1.00, Mistral-7B 0.74 → 1.00, Qwen3-8B 0.99 → 1.00.
- Qwen3-8B, needle planted at token 2048, 64 prompts, concurrency 16: 40k goes from 59/64 to 64/64. 32k stays 64/64 on both arms.
- Short context is unaffected. Qwen3-8B on the same GPU stays within 0.2% at 8k/1k (concurrency 8 and 32) and at 32k/1k. Total tok/s, TTFT, and TPOT all hold.
- The Phi 30k bench is slower on this PR (29,911 → 28,034 tok/s, TTFT 7.27 s → 8.00 s) because main skips the KV. On that bench main leaves 233,430 context tokens unread (28.9% of the KV, 17.1% of prefill attention). This PR reads all 808,402. 574,972 + 233,430 = 808,402.
- The real-backend unordered-batch test fails on `main` and passes here. The all-decode guard is the case #63542 still fails.

## Validation

Image for every run below: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-96710245ece8fe57a0df3ea18cdc79cbb8ce93cf`
(vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev142+g96710245e`). Both arms are that image; the PR arm only bind-mounts
`vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py` and `rocm_aiter_fa.py`. Every log contains
`Using ROCM_AITER_FA backend (selected via --attention-backend)`.

---

## Performance

### 1. Short context — unchanged

A prompt that fits in one chunk never produces the mixed batch this PR fixes, so nothing should
move. Qwen3-8B, same GPU, main then PR:

```bash
# 1x MI300X
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 40960 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching

vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8 --request-rate inf \
  --ignore-eos --seed 2 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot --metric-percentiles 50,99
```

The other rows use the same command with `(8192, 1024, 64, 32)` and `(32768, 1024, 16, 8)`.

| ISL / OSL / conc | prompts | total tok/s | TTFT | TPOT |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1k / 8 | 32 | 6087 → 6094 (+0.1%) | 1.41 → 1.47 s | 10.45 → 10.38 ms |
| 8k / 1k / 32 | 64 | 9966 → 9988 (+0.2%) | 3.10 → 3.09 s | 25.81 → 25.76 ms |
| 32k / 1k / 8 | 16 | 8232 → 8231 (−0.0%) | 6.64 → 6.78 s | 25.54 → 25.40 ms |

Phi-4-mini at 8k behaves the same way (output length 128, concurrency 16, 32 prompts):

| prompt / conc | total tok/s | TTFT | TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8192 / 16 | 34525 → 36201 | 1.38 → 1.25 s | 19.3 → 18.9 ms |

### 2. Long context — Proof that the fix works

Same Phi-4-mini server, prompts long enough that a continuation chunk shares a batch with a fresh
prompt:

| prompt / conc | prompts | total tok/s | TTFT | TPOT |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 30000 / 16 | 16 | 29911 → 28034 (−6.3%) | 7.27 → 8.00 s | 67.1 → 70.0 ms |

Main is faster here because it is doing less work: the rows it misclassifies are attended with
`cu_seqlens_k = query_start_loc`, so `seq − query` tokens of history are never read. The same bench
was rerun with a counter on the prefill slice (`logs/ctx_main.log`, `logs/ctx_pr.log`). Ten chunks
on main were in that state, each a 30k request:

```
q=5424/seq=30000/drop=24576      q=5271/seq=30000/drop=24729      q=5250/seq=30000/drop=24750
q=8088/seq=30000/drop=21912      q=7977/seq=30000/drop=22023      q=7998/seq=30000/drop=22002
q=5331/seq=30000/drop=24669      q=5244/seq=30000/drop=24756
q=8016/seq=30000/drop=21984      q=7971/seq=30000/drop=22029
```

| | context tokens read | context tokens skipped | attention work skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main | 574,972 | 233,430 (28.9%) | 17.1% |
| this PR | 808,402 | 0 | 0 |

574,972 + 233,430 = 808,402: the PR reads exactly the tokens main skips. Main drops 28.9% of the
context, which is 17.1% of the prefill attention work; the MLP still runs on every token, which is
why 17% less attention becomes a 6% throughput gap and a 10% TTFT gap rather than something larger.

The regression is the cost of being correct — the skipped tokens are the dropped history that the
accuracy numbers below measure.

---

## Accuracy

### 1. Short context — unchanged, both correct

Qwen3-8B, needle planted at token 2048 so it sits inside the first 8192-token chunk. 64 prompts,
concurrency 16, greedy. At 32,768 the prompt length is an exact multiple of the chunk budget, so a
fresh prefill and a continuation never share a batch:

| prompt | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 32768 | 64/64 | 64/64 |

### 2. Long context — main loses the needle, the PR does not
`lm_eval niah_single_2` at 30,000 tokens, 500 samples, prompt length 29,990–29,998:

```bash
# 1x MI300X
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks niah_single_2 --batch_size 1 --seed 4321 \
  --model_args model=microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct \
  --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[30000],"tokenizer":"microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct"}' \
  --log_samples --output_path out/
```

| | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| niah_single_2 @ 30k | 0.626 ± 0.022 | 1.000 |

Same recipe across three models, `num_concurrent=16`; each cell logged
`Using ROCM_AITER_FA backend` before the score was counted:

| Model | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Phi-4-mini-instruct | 0.62 | 1.00 |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | 0.74 | 1.00 |
| Qwen3-8B | 0.99 | 1.00 |

Qwen3-8B barely moves; Phi-4-mini and Mistral are the models that expose the bug. The Phi row with
the stderr above is the rerun of that first cell.


### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py::test_rocm_aiter_fa_unordered_batch -v
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_splitting.py tests/v1/worker/test_cp_utils.py -v
```

| test | main | #63542 alone | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test_rocm_aiter_fa_unordered_batch` (2 cases) | 2 failed | — | 2 passed |
| `..._extends[fresh_prompt_sorts_before_extend]` | FAIL | pass | pass |
| `..._extends[all_decode_with_draft_tokens]` | FAIL | FAIL | pass |
| `test_split_dcp_context_queries_counts_a_stale_max_query_len_batch` | FAIL | FAIL | pass |

`split_decodes_prefills_and_extends` has two callers: `rocm_aiter_fa.py` and `cp_utils.py` (NVIDIA DCP). The last row is that second caller. On 8× H200, Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP4, DCP2, FA3, the stock splitter misplaced rows on 24 of 248 calls and this PR on 0. Output under FA3 was 16/16 identical, so that path shows no output change here.

## Details

A batch can contain a fresh prompt before a request that has cached KV. If the splitter assumes
that the first fresh prompt starts the trailing prefill region, it can put the later continuation
on a path that ignores its history. This PR changes how the regions are chosen, sizes the
cached-context chunks correctly, and guards one edge case in the decode count.

### Fix 1 — Find the Last Request with Context

The main cause of the lost-context bug is that MRV2 can place a fresh Prefill request before an
Extend request, while the attention splitter assumes all Extend requests come before Prefill
requests.

As a result, the splitter treats every request after that Prefill as a Prefill too, so the Extend
requests among them are attended without their cached KV history.

To fix this, we find the **last request with cached context** and place the Prefill boundary
immediately after it. Any fresh Prefill requests before this boundary are handled by the Extend
path, which can safely process requests with zero cached context.


### Fix 2 — share the cached-context budget correctly

Because Fix A can place context-free rows in the extend region, the workspace divisor must count
only the rows that actually read context:

```python
num_extends_with_context = max(int((computed_kv_lens > 0).sum()), 1)
max_context_chunk = _CP_TOKENS_PER_ITER_ROCM // num_extends_with_context
```

Dividing by `num_extends` reserves workspace for rows that read nothing, which shrinks everyone
else's chunk and raises `num_chunks = cdiv(max_context, max_context_chunk)`. This is a chunking
change only — it does not alter which rows read their context.

### Fix 3 — Handle All-Decode Batches

There is another edge case where all requests in the attention batch are Decode-like, but
`max_query_len` is larger than the actual query lengths, which can happen during adaptive
speculative verification.

In this case, the original code skips the all-Decode fast path and tries to find the first
non-Decode request. Since no such request exists, `argmax()` returns `0`, incorrectly reporting
zero Decode requests.

**Fix:** We check whether all requests are Decode-like and directly return:

```python
return num_reqs, 0, 0, num_tokens, 0, 0
```

Where:
- `num_reqs`: every request in the batch, all of them Decodes.
- `num_tokens`: every token in the batch, all of them Decode tokens.
- The remaining zeros indicate that there are no Extend or Prefill requests or tokens.

This avoids searching for a non-existent boundary and ensures the entire batch is correctly
processed as Decode.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Dump child process stacks when an AMD CI test times out
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

AMD CI jobs (e.g. V1 Metrics in [build 102446](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102446)) sometimes hang while an EngineCore starts and end with `Timeout (0:25:00)!`, but the dump only shows the pytest process. This makes the `amd_ci_fast_exit` plugin also dump the stacks and kernel wait channels of every child process when a test outlives `faulthandler_timeout`.

## Claims

- When an AMD CI test runs past `faulthandler_timeout` (1500 s), the log now shows each descendant process (including `VLLM::EngineCore` grandchildren): pid/ppid/state/cmdline, per-thread kernel wait channels, and a `py-spy dump --native` stack (gdb fallback).
- Best-effort and bounded (16 processes, 60 s per tool call, 10 min total, 64 KiB per process). It never changes a test result.
- Only affects AMD CI: the plugin is loaded only via `-p amd_ci_fast_exit` in `run-amd-test.sh`. No new dependency (`py-spy==0.4.1` is already in `requirements/test/rocm.txt`, `psutil` in `common.txt`).

## Validation

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fails before (origin/main plugin + new test) | `pytest tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py -k child` | 3/3 failed |
| Passes after, py-spy 0.4.1 on PATH | same | 5/5 passed (`hang_in_child` / `hang_in_grandchild` frames asserted) |
| Passes after, no py-spy or gdb | same | 1/1 passed (wait-channel output still present) |
| Full test file | `pytest tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py` | 13/13 passed |
| Real engine on MI355X (1 GPU) | `LLM(distilgpt2)` test with `-p amd_ci_fast_exit -o faulthandler_timeout=12` | `stacks of 1 child processes`, `VLLM::EngineCore` header, wait channels `futex_wait_queue_me x28, ep_poll x8, ..., kfd_wait_on_events x1`, py-spy stack in `gpu_worker.init_device`; test still passed (exit 0) |
| Lint | `uvx pre-commit run --files <both files>` | all hooks pass |

Manual check of the output: `py-spy --native` showed `clock_nanosleep (libc.so.6)` under `hang_in_child` and `hang_in_grandchild` for both processes.

## Details

**Root cause of the useless dump.** The `Timeout (0:25:00)!` banner is pytest's faulthandler plugin: `run-amd-test.sh` sets `-o faulthandler_timeout=1500` in `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`. It does not kill the job; pytest-timeout (`PYTEST_TIMEOUT=2400`, thread method) does so 15 minutes later. In log 102446 the engine started at 10:14, faulthandler fired at 25 min and pytest-timeout ended the job at about 10:54. Both dumps show only the pytest process, sitting in zmq poll inside `wait_for_engine_startup`. The EngineCore child that actually hangs is never shown, so these 14 hangs in 72 h (all passing on retry) cannot be diagnosed.

**Fix.** A `pytest_runtest_protocol` hookwrapper in `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/amd_ci_fast_exit.py` starts a daemon `threading.Timer` at `faulthandler_timeout + 1` s (covering setup, call and teardown, like faulthandler; the extra second avoids interleaving with faulthandler's output) and cancels it when the test ends. On fire, it walks `psutil.Process().children(recursive=True)` and for each process writes a header (pid, ppid, state, cmdline), a count of `/proc/<pid>/task/*/wchan` values (no ptrace needed; shows waits like `kfd_wait_on_events` or futex), then `py-spy dump --native --pid`, falling back to `gdb -batch -ex 'thread apply all bt'`, else one line saying why the stack dump failed. Everything is in a try/except and writes to the stderr fd saved before pytest captures output. The 10 min budget ends well before the pytest-timeout kill.

New test `tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py`: a test whose child spawns a grandchild and both hang, run with `faulthandler_timeout=1`, asserting both processes get a header and wait-channel line, the dump ends with its closing marker, and (if py-spy or gdb is installed) the `hang_in_child` / `hang_in_grandchild` frames appear.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- py-spy/gdb need ptrace permission on a non-ancestor process. The container here has `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` (`ptrace_scope=1`). If CI pods drop it, the dump prints `stack dump failed: py-spy: exit ...` plus wait channels and cmdline, which still narrows things down but has no stacks.
- py-spy only shows threads with Python frames (native frames merged in). Pure-native HIP/ROCr threads (e.g. rocprofiler queue-intercept threads, the suspected trigger) are visible only through wait-channel counts. Adding gdb to the test-deps stage of `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` would show every native thread; the plugin already uses gdb when py-spy fails. Not added here.
- The dump also fires for tests that are only slow (over 25 min) and then pass. `py-spy dump` briefly pauses each target while reading it; this only adds output and does not change the result.

**Duplicate-work check.** Searched open PRs for `py-spy rocm ci`, `amd_ci_fast_exit`, `faulthandler_timeout`, `stack dump child process timeout ci` and `engine startup hang stack dump`; none covers this. #49628 (opt-in diagnostics for stalled engine stages) is an engine-side feature, not CI tooling. #64752 (skip kineto promotion when `HSA_TOOLS_LIB` is set) is related to the suspected trigger of these hangs but is not a diagnostics change. #67567 also edits `tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py` (signal-state independence); the two changes do not overlap and apply cleanly in either order.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Re-enable VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error in the ROCm test image
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Turns `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` back on in the ROCm test image, so AMD CI flags GPU<->CPU syncs in `execute_model`/`sample_tokens` the same way CUDA CI does (`docker/Dockerfile` sets the same ENV). #61939 dropped the ENV from `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`.

**Depends on #66397, #66400, #66398, #66399. Merge this one last.** Those PRs fix the syncs that failed 16 AMD groups at 8 sites when the check was on ([vllm/ci #97758](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97758), [vllm/amd-ci #15532](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532)). If this lands first, those groups go red again.

This PR reuses #64176. Its first version wrapped all 8 sites in `gpu_sync_allowed()`. `njhill` pointed out that most or all of them could be fixed, so the fixes now live in the four PRs above. This PR keeps only the ENV and the test-instrumentation allow.

## Claims

- `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`: `ENV VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` goes in the per-commit `test` stage, below the `==== per-commit stages: nothing below is part of the runtime key ====` marker. The content-keyed `runtime`/`test-deps` images keep their keys and are not rebuilt.
- `tests/models/test_dsv4{,1}_mono_layers.py`: the `MonoProbe` forward hooks copy decoder-layer outputs and routing margins to the host from inside `execute_model` (`.tolist()`, `.cpu()`). They are test instrumentation, not engine code, so they now run under `gpu_sync_allowed()`. This follows `test_mm_prefix_lm.py` and `test_hisparse.py`. No engine code changes.
  - How these syncs were found: a `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` run of `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py -k 2-8` (TP2, gfx950) with #66397's fix reported only the hook lines (`keep`: `pos.tolist()`, `t[row].float().cpu()`; `gap_hook`: `.tolist()`), apart from the indexer `dcp_rank_tensor` site that #66397 removes.
  - Why allow instead of deferring `.cpu()` to `save_capture()`: the hooks dedupe captures by host position (`setdefault` on `(layer, prompt len, position)`) and read the reused `positions` buffer. Deferring would mean cloning every layer's `(x, residual)` and positions on device every decode step and resolving keys after the run. That is a larger rewrite of test-only code, for no engine benefit.

## Validation

Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), ROCm torch 2.13, amd-aiter 0.1.28.post1.

| Check (this branch) | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py` (Dockerfile/build structure) | 46 passed |
| `pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py --collect-only` | 6 collected |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | passed |

**Integration run on the final stack:** `main` (`5629b26146`) + all commits of #66397, #66400, #66398, #66399, then this PR's two commits, cherry-picked in that order. Each row ran from `tests/` with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. `syncs` = `grep -c "sync detected"` on the log.

The checker is armed only after warmup, inside a worker's `execute_model`/`sample_tokens`. **Armed** rows go through that path, so `0` there is evidence of no syncs. **Not armed** rows call kernels or backends in-process without arming the checker. They are correctness checks only, and their `0` says nothing about syncs.

| Group | Checker | Result | syncs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py::test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[2-8]` (TP2, GPUs 6,7; uses this PR's probe hooks) | armed | 1 passed | 0 |
| `models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3.py` (#66399, GPU 3, see notes) | armed | 6 passed, 1 skipped (needs 2 GPUs) | 0 |
| `/tmp/syncrepro/eplb_rocm_skip_rearrange.py`: EPLB e2e repro, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat TP2 EP (#66399, GPUs 6,7) | armed | `REPRO_OK` | 0 |
| `aiter_gdn_e2e.py`: AITER GDN prefill e2e repro (#66399, GPU 7) | armed | `E2E DONE` (Qwen3.5-0.8B, `Using AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill kernel`) | 0 |
| `models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py -k "int4 and TRITON_ATTN"` (#66399, GPU 3, see notes) | armed | 1 passed, 2 deselected | 0 |
| DiffusionGemma: `v1/sample/test_diffusion_gemma_reads.py v1/sample/test_diffusion_sampler_stats.py v1/worker/test_gpu_diffusion_sampler.py` (#66398, GPU 7) | armed in-process only for the 3 tests in `test_gpu_diffusion_sampler.py` that use the `sync_check_error` fixture; the rest not armed | 49 passed | 0 |
| `v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py -k "rocm or sparse_persistent or sink"` (#66400, GPU 6) | not armed; #66400's sync test stubs `synchronize()` and asserts it is not called | 155 passed, 108 skipped | n/a |
| `models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py` (#66397, GPU 7) | not armed | 15 passed | n/a |
| `tools/test_rocm_build.py` | not armed | 46 passed | n/a |

On this branch alone, without #66397-#66399, the affected groups are expected to fail under the check. Before #66397, the DSv4/DSv4.1 mono groups failed in #97758 with `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected` on every TP worker. That is why this PR has to merge last.

<details>
<summary>Notes on the integration run</summary>

- Every GPU run was serialized with `flock` on a shared host. During part of the run, other containers held about 168 GB on each of GPUs 4-7.
- INT4 on GPU 7 failed before any INT4 engine started. The bf16 baseline `VllmRunner.__init__` (`conftest.py:1027` -> `wait_for_memory_to_settle`) raised `ValueError: Memory of devices devices=[0] not free after dur_s=240.31`, because of that external memory use. There was no sync error. A rerun on GPU 3, which was idle at the time, passed (1 passed, 2 deselected, 0 syncs). An earlier stack showed the same failure in the baseline runner's teardown (`__exit__`), and its rerun also passed.
- Moondream3 on GPU 7 reported 7 skipped. The module fixture converts any `LLM(...)` load failure into `pytest.skip`, and it ran while GPU 7 was under that external memory pressure. A rerun on GPU 3 gave 6 passed, 1 skipped (`Need at least 2 GPUs`).
- An earlier integration run used an earlier revision of #66400 that did not keep persistent AITER metadata for long BF16 prefills. That run hit the pre-existing `large_q_pure_prefill-ROCMAiterMLA` flake (1 failed, 142 passed, 108 skipped), which the current #66400 fixes (pristine main: 3/60 failures, #66400: 0/60). The current stack passes the whole set (row above).
- Exact runner: `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<gpus> CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<gpus> VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 PYTHONPATH=<stack> REPRO_SRC=<stack> flock -w 7200 <lock> timeout 3600 python -m pytest <args> -q`, run from `<stack>/tests`.
</details>

Not covered locally:
- gfx942/MI300.
- Groups that need more than 2 GPUs, including `test_dsv4_mono_layers.py` at TP8.
- Real DeepSeek-V3.2, DSv4-Pro, DiffusionGemma-26B and Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 checkpoints.

AMD CI on this PR, after #66397-#66399 merge, is the full-coverage check. This PR changes no model code, so it needs no model eval of its own. The model evals are in #66397-#66399.

## Details

- The ENV goes in the `test` stage only, so production images (`vllm-openai`) are unaffected. ENV is metadata-only, so the layer is free.
- `_host_reads` is defined in each of the two DSv4 test files. Those files already mirror each other (`_fill`, `RandomWeightLoader`, `MonoProbe`), and a shared helper would add a cross-module import between two standalone test files.
- Not part of this PR: other syncs the check has not reached yet because their groups failed earlier or did not run in #97758/#15532. They are tracked as follow-ups:
  - the MiniMax-M3 epoch-reset `synchronize`
  - the AITER sampler catching `RuntimeError`, which can hide a sync error
  - the MLA gluon/DCP verify `.item()`

  These will be fixed in separate PRs and not wrapped in `gpu_sync_allowed()`.
- Not a duplicate: open PRs were searched for `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`, `gpu_sync_allowed`, "sync rocm" and each site's keywords. #62946 (`aarushjain29`) wraps the INT4 RHT-signs sync in `gpu_sync_allowed()`. #66399 instead builds the signs at attention init, and credits that PR's report. #66003 removes a different sync in the `ROCM_AITER_FA` builder and does not overlap. No other open PR re-enables the check on ROCm.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, write and validate this change.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Model] Run Qwen3.5 on the eager breakable-graph model on MI355X
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds a ROCm variant of the eager Qwen3.5 model (`vllm/models/qwen3_5/amd/`), uses it with breakable CUDA graphs by default on ROCm, and adds an MI355 mirror for the B200 `Qwen3.5` step.

## Claims

- `qwen3_5/amd/model.py`, `amd/mtp.py`: copy of the NVIDIA model with the ROCm counterparts of its fusions: Triton Gemma RMSNorm, the row-parallel all-reduce deferred into AITER's fused all-reduce + Gemma RMSNorm (when AITER custom all-reduce is on), the strided-z GDN gated norm, and the fused QK-norm + RoPE + gate kernel. Keeps AITER fused shared-expert weight rerouting like the legacy ROCm model.
- `qwen3_5/__init__.py`, `config/vllm.py`: ROCm picks the AMD model and adds the Qwen3.5 archs to the ROCm breakable-graph default, on every arch. None of the kernels the AMD model adds needs a specific arch: the Gemma norm, the fused QK-norm + RoPE + gate and the strided-z gated norm are plain Triton, and the AITER fused all-reduce + norm runs only when AITER custom all-reduce is on, with a plain all-reduce + norm fallback.
- `fused_gdn_gated_norm.py` moves from `qwen3_5/nvidia/ops/` to `qwen3_5/common/`, unchanged, since both models use it.
- `qwen3_next.py`: splits the platform-independent `supports_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate` out of `use_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate`. The value of `use_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate` does not change for any model.
- Tests: new `test_amd_model.py` (Qwen3.5-0.8B vs HF greedy logprobs, TP1 Triton path and TP2 AITER path), dispatch and breakable-default cases in `test_qwen3_5.py` and `test_config.py`, the gated-norm tests in `test_gdn_output_projection.py` now also run on ROCm (FP8 output on gfx950), and `test_fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm.py` asserts that the AITER fused all-reduce path is the one taken on ROCm.
- `models_basic.yaml`: `mirror.amd` on `mi355_2` that runs `models/qwen3_5/` plus `kernels/mamba/test_gdn_output_projection.py`.
- `spec_decode.yaml`: the MI355 `Spec Decode MTP Qwen3.5` mirror now also triggers on `vllm/models/qwen3_5/` and `qwen3_next.py`, so changes to `amd/mtp.py` run the MTP e2e tests.

## Validation

All runs on MI355X (gfx950). A reviewer checked gfx942 (model test on both paths, two-module MTP, latency at parity with the compiled model). gfx90a, RDNA and gfx1250 were not run; they take the same path by code reading.

Mirror command, from `tests/`, 2 GPUs, default ROCm CI env:

```bash
pytest -v -s models/qwen3_5/ kernels/mamba/test_gdn_output_projection.py
```

| Run | Result |
|---|---|

Main lands on that tie slightly more often (12.7% vs 10.8% of questions). With the lm_head in fp32 both paths score about 0.87 (main 0.869/0.874, PR 0.886/0.874). Details and the eval fix: #66985. ## Details

On gfx950 the NVIDIA eager model with only a Triton norm was slower than the compiled model, because the q/k Gemma norms and mrope ran unfused in eager mode (about 107 more elementwise kernels per step). With the fused QK-norm + RoPE + gate kernel turned on in the AMD model, it is at parity or a little faster, as the tables show. The one slower cell, TP2 bs32 with AITER (+1.2%), uses AITER's GDN path, which does not call the fused gated norm.

Left out for now. The FP8/NVFP4 norm + input-quant fusions: no ROCm Qwen3.5 checkpoint uses static per-tensor FP8 input scales, and the ROCm-relevant per-token FP8 and MXFP4/MXFP8 variants need their own kernels and evals. The `in_proj_ba` aux-stream overlap stays CUDA-only, because enabling it on ROCm hung in breakable piecewise capture. The model copy follows the `minimax_m3/amd` pattern so the NVIDIA model stays untouched.

This does not duplicate an open PR. Searches for Qwen3.5 with ROCm, AMD, gfx950, MI355 and breakable found no PR that adds a ROCm Qwen3.5 model package. Related PRs that will conflict textually: #51406 enables the fused QK-norm/RoPE/gate kernel in the compiled ROCm path through the same `qwen3_next.py` lines. #66160 edits `fused_gdn_gated_norm.py`, which this PR moves to `common/`. #64687 makes the same kind of port for XPU in `qwen3_5/__init__.py`, `config/vllm.py` and `test_qwen3_5.py`.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Make /ci rocm cache a cache-only CI build that also copies the runtime
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`/ci rocm cache` now runs as a CI build that only copies images, and it copies the PR's runtime and test-deps images along with the stack, so `main` stops rebuilding them after the merge. Rebased onto current `main`; supersedes this PR's earlier version.

## Claims

- The cache build is a `main` build of the ci pipeline that runs only the new `rocm-base-image-cache` step (`VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS`), instead of an AMD CI build. No ci-infra change is needed; ci-infra's AMD CI promote mode (ci-infra#886) can be removed after this merges.
- `build.sh promote` copies the PR's runtime and test-deps images too, so `main` reuses them when it has the same runtime key after the merge. After #65937, `main`'s first build spent 31 min in "Ensure ROCm stack + runtime" (ci build 100464) rebuilding a runtime and test-deps that the PR's CI had already built under those keys.
- Only images the PR's CI build pushed on top of a parent it also pushed are recorded and copied, so a retried job or another PR overwriting this PR's tags can't pair the copied stack with a runtime built on a different one.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py` | 53 passed; the new recording, copy-chain and no-request tests fail on `main`'s `build.sh` |
| `cd .github/workflows/scripts && pytest test_run_ci_command.py` | 74 passed, 117 subtests |
| ci-infra's `pipeline_generator` run on this branch, `main` build with `VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS=["rocm-base-image-cache"]` | exactly one step, queue `amd-cpu`, `ROCM_CI_REPO: rocm/vllm-ci`, no image builds |
| same, nightly (`NIGHTLY=1`) | step included; `promote` exits 0 without `ROCM_PROMOTE_PR` |
| same, normal `main` build | step only offered under "Run more jobs" |
| `pre-commit` on the changed files | clean |

Not run end to end: an actual cache build on the ci pipeline (it needs a PR that changes the ROCm stack and a maintainer's `/ci rocm cache`).

## Details

- `build.sh` base mode records `rocm-rocm-{runtime,test-deps}-built` like `rocm-rocm-stack-built`, but only when the same job also pushed the parent (a `BUILT_HERE` file, since each `ensure` runs in a subshell); building a stack resets both to `none`, because metadata outlives a retried job. `promote` copies stack-wheels, stack, runtime, test-deps in order, each child only over a parent this run copied, never over an image `main` built; a missing child record stops the chain with exit 0.
- The step lives in `.buildkite/image_build/amd_rocm_cache.yaml`. ci-infra's AMD CI pipeline renders every file in `hardware_tests/`, but only the main pipeline lists `image_build/`. It is optional. Nightlies still run optional steps, so without a request `promote` exits 0 right after its arguments, before the builder, build context or tag fetch. It also validates the PR number and commit format that ci-infra's `bootstrap-amd.sh` used to check.
- The handler still looks for the source build in both pipelines, since PRs still run AMD CI (#66596's cache came from an AMD CI build).
- Limits: if `main` changes a runtime-key input (requirements, `Dockerfile.rocm` above the marker) between the PR's CI build and the merge, the copied runtime is unused and `main` rebuilds it as before (#66596: 46 min). A retried promote finishes the chain: an existing tag holding the digest the PR's CI recorded is an earlier attempt's copy, and only a different digest is treated as `main`'s.

## Overview DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash does not run on A100 today: its attention, indexer and cache codecs need FlashMLA, DeepGEMM and FP8/FP4 conversion instructions that SM80 lacks; on H100, `main` runs it on its stock kernels. This PR serves the model on one 8×A100 or 8×H100 node with decode kernels written in CuTe DSL, all under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/`; other GPUs keep their current path. Accuracy is on par with `main` on GB300, and in AgentX H100 reaches 1.5–1.7× the P90 interactivity of InferenceX's H100 vLLM line. ![DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash AgentX on 8×H100 and 8×A100, this PR against InferenceX's H100 vLLM line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yaoyaoding/vllm/19f66703fce5da5fc12b706a6525d3adb2040fcc/sm80_sm90_agentx.png) ## Claims - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serves on 8×A100 (SM80) at TP8, with DSpark speculative decoding. - On 8×H100 (SM90), the decode path reaches 489 P90 tok/s per user at one request in AgentX, against 324 for InferenceX's H100 vLLM line. - Accuracy on both matches `main` on GB300 (GSM8K, GPQA-Diamond, AIME25, RULER NIAH up to 256K). ## Validation ### Accuracy Stock vLLM does not run DeepSeek-V4.1 on A100, so the reference is `main` on one GB300 tray as measured for #63921 (same checkpoint, tasks and sampling). ### AgentX InferenceX's AgentX client, TP8, DSpark with 5 drafts at InferenceX's synthetic acceptance length (3.51), `max-num-seqs` 32. TPOT | Concurrency | H100 TPOT p50 / p90 (ms) | A100 TPOT p50 / p90 (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 1.97 / 2.05 | 2.82 / 3.13 | | 4 | 1.98 / 2.51 | 2.95 / 3.83 | | 8 | 2.26 / 3.12 | 3.62 / 5.17 | | 16 | 2.91 / 4.65 | 4.98 / 8.37 | | 20 | 3.48 / 4.84 | | | 24 | 4.11 / 6.77 | | | 28 | 5.01 / 9.03 | | | 32 | 6.28 / 12.91 | 8.09 / 16.98 | From c4 on, p50 barely moves while p90 grows: vLLM's scheduler mixes a long prompt's prefill chunks into the running decode steps, and those steps set p90. No failed requests and no empty responses.
## Details
What changed ### SM80 kernels (`nvidia/specialized_decode/ampere/`), also used by SM90 | Module | Contents | | --- | --- | | `attention.py` | `DeepseekV41AmpereAttention`, its compressor and its metadata backends | | `sparse_mla.py` | Sparse MLA for decode and prefill tokens alike: each token attends to its window keys and its indexer-selected compressed keys; a variant reads H100's V4 records | | `indexer.py`, `indexer_metadata.py`, `mqa_logits.py` | The MXFP4 indexer: query and key quantization, its op and metadata builder, ragged, paged and candidate-only logits (MXFP4 or FP8 keys) | | `row_shard.py` | The indexer's prefill row split over the TP ranks, shared with SM90 | | `topk.py` | The indexer's decode top-k and candidate-block selection, over each row's own length, split over CTAs for long rows | | `gemv.py` | MXFP8 decode GEMV over a packed FP8 copy of the dense weights | | `quantize.py` | MXFP4 index-key and query quantizers, NVFP4 compressed-record writer | | `mhc.py` | The mHC layer boundary: post-mix, collapse + RMSNorm, and the next boundary's coefficients (on tensor cores on SM80) | | `all_reduce.py` | The boundaries' two-shot Lamport all-reduce: alone, fused with the mHC post-collapse, and taking the MoE's top-k finalize | | `all_gather.py` | The Lamport all-gather: the indexer's row-split decode top-k (rank-major), the logits and Engram columns (side by side) | | `columns.py` | The gathers along the last dimension: one per row size, `AmpereLogitsProcessor`, the Engram hook | | `codecs.py` | Device helpers: FP8 and FP4 decode and encode, raw loads and stores | - **KV cache.** On SM80 the cache keeps the SM100 records: 528-byte MXFP8 sliding-window records, 288-byte NVFP4 compressed records and 68-byte MXFP4 index keys. - **Sparse MLA.** One partial kernel splits each token's key list over CTAs in 64-key chunks, and a merge kernel adds the attention sink, normalizes, and applies the inverse RoPE. Each chunk is gathered in one memory round trip. FP8 and FP4 key codes decode in pairs straight into BF16x2 words, bit-identical to decoding through FP32. The kernel computes S^T = K Q^T and O^T = V^T P^T, so a rank's 8 heads at TP8 fill an 8-wide N tile with no padding rows. A launch with one split per token finishes its rows in the kernel and skips the merge. - **Indexer decode.** CUDA graphs fix a decode row's width at the model length (1M tokens), and the stock path sized its logits grid and top-k by that width. Here: - the paged logits kernel splits each row's own length over one wave of CTAs and shares one CTA among the rows of a request in uniform speculative decode; - the candidate consumers (layers 24, 28, 32, 36) score only the 2048 × 8 keys of their candidate blocks, in compact rows, instead of the whole context with a mask; - the decode top-k selects each row's top k over its own length (a radix select, ties to the lowest index), and rows wider than one CTA's chunk split over CTAs and merge; its workspace is in the profile reservation. Its first digit pass keeps a CTA's keys (one chunk at most, 64 KB) in shared memory, interleaved across threads, and the later passes and the writes read them there instead of re-reading global memory. Prefill keeps vLLM's top-k, as do top-k backends other than `auto`. - **Decode GEMV.** The MXFP8 linear layers keep the BF16 weight that vLLM's emulation kernel dequantizes at load, for cuBLAS, and also a packed copy of the FP8 weight (about 1.2 GB per GPU at TP8). Decode steps of up to 24 rows run a CuTe DSL GEMV over the packed copy, which reads half the bytes: one layer's five dense GEMMs on H100 take 25.1 µs against cuBLAS's 38.4 at 6 rows. The codes decode exactly with integer operations, the column split reduces in a fixed order, and a weight reload rewrites the copy in place so captured graphs keep their address. - **mHC boundary.** Two CuTe DSL kernels replace TileLang at small boundaries: `PostCollapse` (post-mix, stored residual, collapse with RMSNorm) on the critical path, and `Coefficients` (the next boundary's mixes and Sinkhorn normalization) on the side stream inside FULL graphs. SM80 takes them up to 256 rows, SM90 up to 48. `Coefficients` holds 40 SMs at any batch: a CTA per 128-column slice walks the 16-row groups, so `PostCollapse`'s 640-thread CTAs always find free SMs (at 48 rows a CTA per slice and group would take 120 CTAs, more than A100's 108 SMs). On SM80 the coefficients run on tensor cores: `CoefficientsMma` projects on `mma.sync` BF16 in hidden / 320 = 16 CTAs, each FP32 weight split into two BF16 terms (about 16 significand bits, more than SM90's stock TF32 projection). SM90 keeps the CUDA-core kernel, where the tensor-core one made B=1 1.7% slower. - **Indexer row split.** Under TP every rank scored every indexer row, and on SM80 the scoring runs on BF16 tensor cores. A step's prefill rows split over the ranks once their scoring work (rows × compressed keys) reaches 2^22, the candidate rows included: every indexer of a step narrows by the same metadata, so a rank's candidate consumers read only the blocks its own source wrote. `main`'s shared builder no longer splits (#63956), so `row_shard.py` keeps the balanced split, the narrowed prefill chunks and the top-k exchange that #54951 added, for SM80 and SM90. Pure-decode steps of at least two requests give each rank ceil(B / TP) whole requests, and the ranks' int32 top-k rows are gathered back into the step's buffer (in place, by the Lamport all-gather below). - **Prefill mHC projection.** Above 256 rows the boundaries projected with the stock TileLang kernel on CUDA cores (about 0.5 ms per boundary at a 4,096-token chunk on A100), because DeepGEMM's split-k projection has no SM80 build. `MhcProjection` projects on `mma.sync` BF16 tensor cores instead, with each FP32 weight split into two BF16 terms (about 16 significand bits, more than DeepGEMM's TF32), and the stock pre-norm epilogue adds its per-split partial sums as it does DeepGEMM's. - **MXFP8 linears and routed MoE.** On SM80 and SM90 the MXFP8 linears run as BF16 GEMMs (the platforms' MXFP8 kernels were slower at every batch size), and the Marlin MXFP4 experts pad the per-rank intermediate size to 64 instead of 128 (288 → 320 at TP8, not 384). Marlin is vLLM's default on SM80; on SM90 it runs with `--moe-backend marlin`. - **TP collectives on SM80.** vLLM's custom all-reduce inside `wo_b` and the MoE is latency-bound at decode sizes on A100 (about 28 µs a call at 24 rows on 8×A100, waits for the other ranks included). - `TwoShotAllReduce` (CuTe DSL) pushes instead and synchronizes through the data: one CTA per row; each 16-byte fragment goes to the rank owning its slice, which adds the slice in FP32 in a fixed butterfly order and pushes the BF16 sum to every rank. BF16 negative zero is the Lamport sentinel, each row keeps three generations of slots in a symmetric-memory mailbox, and every rank gets the same bits. The boundaries take the all-reduce (`wo_b` and the MoE leave it to them, as on SM90), up to 128 rows (B=16 with five drafts is 96), at most one CTA per SM. - The same CTA then runs the boundary's post-mix, collapse and RMSNorm (`TwoShotAllReducePostCollapse`): bitwise the two kernels, one launch and one round trip of the sublayer output fewer. - SM80 defers the MoE's top-k reduction as SM90 does with Marlin (`DeferringMarlinExperts`): the boundary forms each rank's partial row from the unweighted GEMM2 rows, the FP32 routing weights and the shared expert's row (an FP32 fused multiply-add per route, one BF16 rounding, as SM90's kernel), so `moe_sum` and the shared add go away. - The indexer's row-split decode gathers its top-k rows with `AllGatherRows`, a push-based Lamport all-gather per (row, hop) with INT32_MIN as the sentinel, straight into the shared top-k buffer: each rank scores its share in place, with no private share and no copy. - The two-shot kernel also takes the eleven TP all-reduces of a step that would go through vLLM's custom all-reduce (0.15–0.39 ms a step at B1–B16): the DSpark draft model's layer boundaries (its layers are built with the fused all-reduce; their top-3 MoE still finalizes itself) and tail, the input embedding shared by both models (built with `reduce_results=False` and reduced by `embed_input_ids`), the boundary before each Engram layer, and the target's tail before the head. - The logits of the target and the draft model, and each Engram layer's TP-sharded heads and `wkv` output, are gathered side by side by the same all-gather (`columns.py`), each row written in place with every rank's columns. vLLM gathers them with NCCL's ring into rank-major blocks and then copies the blocks side by side: at B16 about 170 + 60 µs for a step's logits and 35 + 70 µs for an Engram layer. The Engram layer takes the gather through an optional hook, `Engram.set_column_gather` in `common/engram.py` (unset by default, so other platforms are unchanged). ### SM90 (`nvidia/specialized_decode/hopper/` and the model package) - **Decode attention.** H100 keeps DeepSeek's V4 KV records (448 E4M3 dims with a UE8M0 scale per 64, then 64 BF16 RoPE dims). `DeepseekV41HopperAttention`, a subclass of the FlashMLA layer, runs decode tokens through the sparse MLA variant that reads them: the rank's 8 heads unpadded (FlashMLA needs 64), no split planning and no combine kernel. Prefill stays on FlashMLA. An explicit attention backend keeps the stock layer. - **Routed MoE.** The routed experts keep vLLM's choice on SM90: Humming, running the checkpoint's MXFP8 activations as block FP8. With `--moe-backend marlin` the Marlin experts take the 64-padding above and the deferred reduction below. - **Fused all-reduce at the mHC boundary.** At TP8 with NVLink multicast, a boundary of up to 12 rows inside FULL graphs runs `AllReduceMHC`, the Lamport all-reduce fused with the mHC post-mix, collapse and RMSNorm, as SM100 does at TP4. The fused kernel is one-shot, and vLLM's own all-reduce switches to two-shot above 12 rows of this model, where two-shot wins; larger boundaries all-reduce first. - **Deferred MoE reduction.** With the Marlin experts, within the fused rows, `DeferringMarlinExperts` return GEMM2's unweighted rows, and `AllReduceMHC.finalize` weights and sums them and adds the shared expert inside the all-reduce, so `moe_sum` and the separate add go away. LoRA keeps the finalized path. - **Indexer.** `HopperIndexer` keeps vLLM's op except on steps of only decode rows: the candidate consumers run the compact kernels above on SM90's FP8 index cache, and the candidate source (layer 20) keeps DeepGEMM's logits and the stock top-k but selects its 2048 blocks with the specialized decode's cooperative selection over each row's length instead of `torch.topk` over the whole 1M-token width. - **Indexer prefill row split.** The SM90 index K cache names its own metadata builder, which splits a step's prefill rows over the ranks once their scoring work reaches 2^24. `HopperIndexer` narrows the stock op's prefill chunks to the rank's rows and gathers the top-k rows back; the candidate rows stay replicated. - **Column gathers and the draft's fused boundaries.** H100 gathers the logits of the target and the draft model, and the Engram heads and `wkv` output, with SM80's side-by-side Lamport all-gather (`columns.py`) instead of NCCL's ring and a copy. The DSpark draft layers take SM90's fused `AllReduceMHC` at their boundaries, up to its 12 rows (one or two requests); larger boundaries all-reduce first, as the target's do. ### Both - **Recorded metadata builds.** Before every FULL decode replay the runner built the attention metadata eagerly, about 40 small launches per H100 step (~260 µs at one request, mostly launch gaps). The specialized decode already records these builds as CUDA graphs; `DeepseekV41MetadataGraphModelState` does it for SM80 and SM90 too. - **Fused Markov loop by default.** `main`'s fused Markov loop (#64442) is on by default on SM80 and SM90 (`dspark_fused_markov: false` turns it off). - **Stress mode.** Run as modules with `--replays N`, `test_all_reduce.py` and `test_all_gather.py` replay CUDA graphs of collectives of different sizes, some with the ranks skewed, in one seeded random order with new contents every replay, and count every wrong element on the device. The all-reduce inputs are small integers whose sum over the ranks takes 61 values depending on the element, the replay and the call, so a stale, misplaced or missing write shows up.
Placement New kernels and subclasses sit under `nvidia/specialized_decode/ampere/` and `nvidia/specialized_decode/hopper/`, the quantization choices in `nvidia/quantization.py`, and the remaining edits in the model package (`nvidia/model.py`, `nvidia/dspark.py`, `nvidia/ops/mhc.py`, `specialized_decode/runtime/`, `attention.py`, `common/engram.py`, `quant_config.py`). Two files outside it change: - `tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py` (9 lines): the TP4 cases of the fused all-reduce gate test stub an SM100 platform, because the gate now depends on the GPU. - `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`: the optional 8×H100 step (19 lines) that runs this PR's tests.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Compare logprobs in the Machete bf16 repeat-run test
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantization` Shard 2/4 flakes on main (102839, 103085; about 2 of 38 builds):

```
quantization/test_cutlass_w4a16.py::test_w4a16_machete_bfloat16_deterministic
AssertionError: Non-deterministic: 'Tuesday, the day of the first day of' vs 'Tuesday, the day after the 10'
```

The test runs the same 6-token prompt twice at batch size 1 and asserts that the two greedy outputs match exactly. vLLM only guarantees bitwise-identical repeated runs in batch-invariant mode. This tiny 4-bit model has near-tied logits; the outputs split at token 5 after a nonsense continuation. Machete's CUTLASS StreamK scheduler isn't the source: CUTLASS v4.7.1 defaults to `ReductionMode::Deterministic`, and Machete keeps that default. I haven't pinned down exactly which step differs between the two runs; that would need logit dumps on a MIG slice.

The test now compares `generate_greedy_logprobs` (top-5) of the two runs with `check_logprobs_close`. A broken kernel still fails it, because its tokens would fall outside each other's top-k, and the test still checks that Machete is the selected kernel.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `test_w4a16_machete_bfloat16_deterministic` and found none.

## Test Plan

- CI: `quantization` (H200 MIG 35GB).
- `pre-commit run --files tests/quantization/test_cutlass_w4a16.py`

## Test Result

- pre-commit passes.
- CI result will be added below.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed the change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Fall back to torch.distributed when pynccl is disabled
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

I hit a silent precision failure in model-level sequence parallelism: when pynccl is disabled (for example, when the installed NCCL is older than 2.29.7 and lacks `ncclCommSuspend`), `CudaCommunicator.reduce_scatter` still allocates its output with `torch.empty` and calls a disabled `PyNcclCommunicator.reduce_scatter`, which returns without writing anything. The caller gets uninitialized memory. This PR falls back to the base-class `torch.distributed` reduce-scatter when pynccl is unavailable, and logs a one-time warning at communicator construction so the silent performance downgrade and the upgrade path are visible.

## Claims

- `CudaCommunicator.reduce_scatter` now returns a correct result when pynccl is `None` or `disabled`: it falls back to `DeviceCommunicatorBase.reduce_scatter` (`torch.distributed.reduce_scatter_tensor`), matching the reference bit-for-bit in the reproducer below.
- The pynccl fast path is unchanged when pynccl is healthy; this only affects the unavailable/disabled case.
- `PyNcclCommunicator.__init__` logs a one-time warning when it disables itself, including the original exception and the "upgrade to NCCL >= 2.29.7 if this is due to an old NCCL" hint. The warning is at startup, not on the `reduce_scatter` hot path.
- Added `test_reduce_scatter_falls_back_when_pynccl_disabled`, which mocks the base-class method and asserts the fallback is used with the right arguments.
- This does not loosen the NCCL version requirement: CUDA still needs NCCL >= 2.29.7 for pynccl, and `ncclCommSuspend` remains required. It also does not change `reduce_scatterv`, which already asserts loudly when pynccl is disabled.
- On a 2048-token real Chinese-text prompt, I measured the broken path emitting markdown/URL fragments (`![](https://... document.body...`) with all 2047 prompt logprobs equal to `-11.95041`, while the pynccl-enabled reference produced coherent text with 1902 distinct logprobs. The same-prompt difference was mean **10.00994 nats**, max **11.95041**, with 2034 of 2047 positions off by >1 nat and different output tokens.

## Validation

### How I hit it

I was validating model-level SP with HiSparse on GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 (8xH20, TP8+EP8, torch 2.14.0+cu126 with NCCL 2.29.3). Small probes (<=16 MiB per reduce-scatter, roughly <=1365 tokens) were clean, which made it look like an SP or HiSparse accuracy bug. At 2048 tokens the layer-0 `pre_norm` dump from the broken path differed from the fixed path by **4.3394x in absmean**, with **99.972% of elements differing**; teacher-forced prompt-logprob deltas were **0.63-0.69 nats** on the broken path vs **0.105-0.124 nats** after the fix (1K/4K/8K/16K/32K/64K/128K), and GSM8K-200 was 0.915/0.910 with no NaN after the fix. The size threshold was the clue: <=16 MiB uses the custom MNNVL Lamport reduce-scatter, above it goes through `CudaCommunicator.reduce_scatter`.

### How I narrowed it down

My first guess was double-sharding or a HiSparse/SP interaction, because the failure only appeared once the model-level SP path was enabled and small tests looked fine. Two things did not fit that guess: the magnitude was far too large for a reduction-order difference, and the bad values looked like stale memory rather than a slightly different sum. I checked the pynccl startup log and saw that the usual "vLLM is using nccl==" line was missing, which meant `PyNcclCommunicator` had been silently disabled. Reading `CudaCommunicator.reduce_scatter` showed that it only asserted `pynccl_comm is not None`; it never checked `disabled`. Reading `PyNcclCommunicator.reduce_scatter` showed the early `if self.disabled: return`, so the `torch.empty` output was never written. The >16 MiB threshold matched exactly where the custom MNNVL path stops and the pynccl path starts, which closed the loop.

### Root cause

The environment pins `torch==2.14.0+cu126`, which requires `nvidia-nccl-cu12==2.29.3`. This vLLM revision's pynccl wrapper resolves `ncclCommSuspend`, which needs NCCL >= 2.29.7; 2.29.3 does not export it, so `NCCLLibrary(...)` raises and `PyNcclCommunicator` sets `disabled=True`. The old `CudaCommunicator.reduce_scatter` allocated `output = torch.empty(...)` and called `pynccl_comm.reduce_scatter(output, input_tensor)`; the disabled communicator returned immediately, and the caller used whatever was in the uninitialized block. I want to be precise about one thing: the earlier NaN episode was a different, early double-sharding revision; this failure produced garbage/precision collapse, and the disabled pynccl is the cause.

### Reproducer (2 GPUs)

The reproducer forces `PyNcclCommunicator.disabled=True` with `library_path="/nonexistent/libnccl.so"` (the same disabled state the old NCCL produces), builds a `CudaCommunicator` with a real NCCL process group, computes the reference with `torch.distributed.reduce_scatter_tensor`, then runs the pre-fix default path and the fixed path. To make the uninitialized output visible, it fills a same-shape tensor with `12345.0` and frees it before the old path allocates its `torch.empty`, so the caching allocator hands that block back.

Run:

```bash
torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 repro_pynccl_disabled.py
```

Output from 2 ranks:

```
rank=1 buggy_ok=False fixed_ok=True buggy_max=12348.4 fixed_max=0 buggy_all_sentinel=True buggy_sample=[12345.0, 12345.0, 12345.0] ref_sample=[0.9995849, -0.6163927, 2.1244459]
rank=0 buggy_ok=False fixed_ok=True buggy_max=12348.8 fixed_max=0 buggy_all_sentinel=True buggy_sample=[12345.0, 12345.0, 12345.0] ref_sample=[-0.8856844, 0.2670063, -0.4641280]
ALL_RANKS buggy_ok=False fixed_ok=True bug_reproduced=True
```

`buggy_all_sentinel=True` means the old path returned the `12345` block untouched; `fixed_max=0` means the fallback matches the reference exactly. The script is in the details below; it needs 2 GPUs, so it is a manual validation rather than a CI test. The committed unit test covers the same branch with mocks.

### Model-level reproducer

The trigger is SP calling `reduce_scatter` with a tensor above 16 MiB, not the prompt content. On main, HiSparse on disables ShardQ (`use_shardq` requires `hisparse_config is None`), and model-level SP requires every layer to use ShardQ, so HiSparse on cannot take this path. The command below is stock main with HiSparse off, which is the configuration where model-level SP is enabled. The bug is not HiSparse-specific or ShardQ-specific: any SP caller that sends more than 16 MiB through `CudaCommunicator.reduce_scatter` while pynccl is disabled is affected; `use_sequence_parallel_moe` and the other SP callers go through the same collective. 16 MiB / (hidden size 6144 x 2 bytes) is about 1365 tokens, so a 2048-token prefill is enough; 1024 tokens stays on the custom MNNVL path and looks fine.

The configuration is GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 on 8xH20, TP8+EP8, max-model-len 8192, max-num-batched-tokens 8192, max-num-seqs 64, gpu-memory-utilization 0.92, fp8_ds_mla KV, cutlass MoE, prefix cache off. To force the disabled pynccl path on any NCCL version, set `VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL=1`; the original trigger was the environment's torch 2.14.0+cu126 with NCCL 2.29.3, which disables pynccl because it lacks `ncclCommSuspend`. Run this on the parent commit to see the bug; on this PR the same command falls back to `torch.distributed`.

```bash
VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL=1 vllm serve <GLM-5.3-W4AFP8> \
  --served-model-name GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --moe-backend cutlass \
  --scheduler-reserve-full-isl \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --attention-config '{"sparse_mla_shard_q": true}' \
  --port 8021
```

Confirm the SP path is active in the serve log:

```
Sharding sparse MLA prefill steps of >= 1024 tokens across TP ranks by token.
```

Send the 2048-token prompt (random non-special token IDs, seed 97001; the prompt SHA in my runs is `a0c2c2721a452e80`):

```python
import random

import requests
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("<GLM-5.3-W4AFP8>", trust_remote_code=True)
rng = random.Random(97001)
special = set(tok.all_special_ids)
vocab = [i for i in range(len(tok)) if i not in special]
prompt = [rng.choice(vocab) for _ in range(2048)]
r = requests.post(
    "http://127.0.0.1:8021/v1/completions",
    json={
        "model": "GLM-5.3-W4AFP8",
        "prompt": prompt,
        "max_tokens": 1,
        "temperature": 0,
        "prompt_logprobs": 0,
        "ignore_eos": True,
        "return_token_ids": True,
    },
    timeout=600,
)
print(r.status_code, r.text[:200])
```

Run the same prompt twice on the parent commit: once with `VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL=1`, once with pynccl enabled (NCCL >= 2.29.7, no env var), and compare `prompt_logprobs`. The broken run differs by about 0.63-0.69 nats; the pynccl-enabled run is the reference. With this PR, the `VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL=1` run matches the pynccl-enabled run within the normal ~0.105-0.124 nats A/A noise. The 1024-token prompt is the negative control: it is below 16 MiB and stays on the custom MNNVL path. In my validation the 2048-token layer-0 `pre_norm` dump differed by 4.3394x absmean with 99.972% of elements differing.

### Real-text A/B

The random-token probe is deterministic, but the same failure is much more visible on real text. I sent a 2048-token prefix of a Chinese novel to the same server. The broken run produced `![](https://www.jpg.com">, the">, the">the the">the the document.body">the1">the document.body">the document` and had all 2047 prompt logprobs equal to `-11.95041` (one unique value; the output starts with token 0, which decodes to `!`). The pynccl-enabled reference produced a coherent Chinese continuation and 1902 distinct prompt logprobs; its first few were `-10.03958, -9.882, -2.81865, -0.06047, -0.0005`. The same-prompt prompt-logprob difference was mean **10.00994 nats**, max **11.95041**, with 2045 positions >0.1 and 2034 >1.0, and the output tokens differed. Natural text has higher-confidence tokens, which is why the mean delta is larger than the random-token probe's 0.69 nats; the trigger is still the same 2048-token prefill.

### Startup warning

Constructing `PyNcclCommunicator` with a bad library path prints:

```
PyNcclCommunicator is disabled; vLLM will fall back to torch.distributed collectives, which can be slower. If this is due to an old NCCL, upgrade to >= 2.29.7: ...
```

and the communicator ends up `available=False`, `disabled=True`. The warning is emitted at construction (startup) with `warning_once`; the `reduce_scatter` path itself is log-free.

### Unit test

`pytest tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py::test_reduce_scatter_falls_back_when_pynccl_disabled` mocks `DeviceCommunicatorBase.reduce_scatter` and asserts the fallback gets `(input_, dim)` when `pynccl_comm.disabled=True`. The 2-rank reproducer above exercises the same path end to end.

## Details

- Trigger conditions: model-level SP calls `sp_reduce_scatter` every layer; tensors <=16 MiB use the custom MNNVL Lamport path and are correct, above that they go through `CudaCommunicator.reduce_scatter`. The failure therefore only appears on larger token counts, which is why small tests looked fine. On main, HiSparse on blocks ShardQ and therefore model-level SP; the reproducer above uses HiSparse off, which is the stock configuration where model-level SP is enabled. Any SP caller with >16 MiB and disabled pynccl is affected.
- Why this needs a code change instead of an environment note: side-installing NCCL 2.29.7 via `VLLM_NCCL_SO_PATH` fixes one deployment, but any user on an older NCCL, a missing library, or `VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL` still gets silent corruption. `all_gather` already checks `pynccl_comm is None or pynccl_comm.disabled` and falls back; `reduce_scatter` was the outlier. The correctness fix has to live in the code, and the startup warning is how users learn they are on the slower path. Documentation alone cannot enforce it.
- Design: mirror the existing `all_gather` fallback; do not loosen the NCCL version requirement or make `ncclCommSuspend` optional; keep `reduce_scatterv`'s loud assertion; log once at `PyNcclCommunicator` construction, not in the hot path.
- Tradeoffs and limitations: the fallback uses `torch.distributed`, which can be slower than pynccl; the warning says so and points at NCCL >= 2.29.7. The change is limited to the disabled/unavailable pynccl case; healthy pynccl behavior is untouched. The reproducer is a manual 2-GPU script; the committed test is the mock-based unit test. The old path in the reproducer is a line-by-line replica of the pre-fix default CUDA branch (no batch-invariant, no symm-mem), which is the path that failed here.

<details>
<summary>2-GPU reproducer</summary>

```python
import os

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.cuda_communicator import CudaCommunicator
from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.pynccl import PyNcclCommunicator
from vllm.distributed.utils import StatelessProcessGroup


def old_reduce_scatter(comm, input_, dim=-1):
    # Default CUDA path from before the fix: allocate output with torch.empty,
    # then call pynccl. A disabled pynccl returns without writing output.
    world_size = comm.world_size
    pynccl_comm = comm.pynccl_comm
    assert pynccl_comm is not None
    if dim < 0:
        dim += input_.dim()
    input_tensor = input_.movedim(0, dim).contiguous()
    assert input_tensor.shape[0] % world_size == 0
    chunk_size = input_tensor.shape[0] // world_size
    output_shape = (chunk_size,) + input_tensor.shape[1:]
    output = torch.empty(
        output_shape, dtype=input_tensor.dtype, device=input_tensor.device
    )
    pynccl_comm.reduce_scatter(output, input_tensor)
    return output.movedim(0, dim).contiguous()


def main():
    rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
    world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
    torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
    dist.init_process_group("nccl", rank=rank, world_size=world_size)
    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}")

    fake_group = object.__new__(StatelessProcessGroup)
    fake_group.rank = rank
    fake_group.world_size = world_size
    pynccl = PyNcclCommunicator(
        fake_group, device=device, library_path="/nonexistent/libnccl.so"
    )
    assert pynccl.disabled, "expected pynccl to be disabled"

    comm = CudaCommunicator.__new__(CudaCommunicator)
    comm.world_size = world_size
    comm.rank = rank
    comm.device_group = dist.group.WORLD
    comm.pynccl_comm = pynccl

    torch.manual_seed(2026 + rank)
    x = torch.randn(world_size * 8, 16, device=device)
    ref = torch.empty(8, 16, device=device)
    dist.reduce_scatter_tensor(ref, x, group=dist.group.WORLD)

    junk = torch.full((8, 16), 12345.0, device=device)
    del junk
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    buggy = old_reduce_scatter(comm, x, 0)
    fixed = comm.reduce_scatter(x, 0)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    buggy_ok = torch.equal(buggy, ref)
    fixed_ok = torch.equal(fixed, ref)
    buggy_max = (buggy - ref).abs().max().item()
    fixed_max = (fixed - ref).abs().max().item()
    sentinel_all = bool((buggy == 12345.0).all().item())
    print(
        f"rank={rank} buggy_ok={buggy_ok} fixed_ok={fixed_ok} "
        f"buggy_max={buggy_max:.6g} fixed_max={fixed_max:.6g} "
        f"buggy_all_sentinel={sentinel_all} "
        f"buggy_sample={buggy.flatten()[:3].tolist()} "
        f"ref_sample={ref.flatten()[:3].tolist()}",
        flush=True,
    )
    flags = torch.tensor(
        [1.0 if buggy_ok else 0.0, 1.0 if fixed_ok else 0.0], device=device
    )
    dist.all_reduce(flags, op=dist.ReduceOp.MIN)
    if rank == 0:
        bug_reproduced = not bool(flags[0].item())
        fix_ok = bool(flags[1].item())
        print(
            f"ALL_RANKS buggy_ok={bool(flags[0].item())} fixed_ok={fix_ok} "
            f"bug_reproduced={bug_reproduced}",
            flush=True,
        )
        assert bug_reproduced, "bug did not reproduce"
        assert fix_ok, "fixed path does not match reference"
    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

commits.pr_title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Cap dummy-run requests by their draft slots
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With draft-model speculative decoding, engine startup fails with an `AssertionError` whenever `max_num_seqs * 2 > max_num_batched_tokens`, e.g. `--max-num-batched-tokens 256` with the default `max_num_seqs`. `_dummy_run` keeps `num_reqs = min(num_tokens, max_num_reqs)` and then takes one draft slot per request out of the token budget, which can leave fewer tokens than requests. This caps `num_reqs` the same way #65270 capped warmup.

## Claims

- draft_model starts and generates at 256/256, 128/128 and 256/200 (`max_num_batched_tokens`/`max_num_seqs`), which crash on main. Configs that already started are unchanged.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`: the new test fails 2 of 5 cases on main. The file passes (37) with the fix.
- RTX 4090, Qwen3-1.7B with a Qwen3-0.6B draft, k=3: all three configs start and generate, and under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` greedy output matches the non-speculative run bit for bit.

## Details

No open issue or PR covers this. #65856 and #65270 fixed the same pattern in warmup.
