commits.pr_title: [Model] Add opt-in PrimTS attention for Step5 on Blackwell
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add opt-in PrimTS DSA and sliding-window attention for Step5 on Blackwell (SM100/103/107), supporting BF16 and pure E4M3 QKV. Requires FlashInfer 0.7.4, which ships [FlashInfer #6925](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6925) and [#7106](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/7106); main already pins `flashinfer-python==0.7.4`, so this PR does not change requirements. Builds on #61727.

## Claims

- Native remains the default. When enabled, PrimTS handles supported prefill; BF16 decode uses PrimTS at captured/padded batch size ≥32 with MTP=3. FP8 decode always uses PrimTS.
- Reuses existing cache producers, selectors and gate. FP8 Q quantization is fused into the Q/KV producer, with output retained in the model activation dtype.
- SWA uses the runtime-length FlashInfer `max_q_len` API. Logical Q/KV capacities remain planning/workspace bounds, while compiled attention is reused across changing lengths.
- Fixed-Q decode derives metadata from KV lengths; packed prefill shares asynchronously uploaded grouping offsets across layers. Scheduler and CUDA-graph padding behavior are unchanged. Upstream native SM100 admission is preserved.
- FlashInfer 0.7.4 renames several prims_ts arguments (`q_data_type`→`q_dtype`, `o_data_type`→`out_dtype`, `use_packed_q`→`packed_query`, `sm_scale`/`bmm1_scale`→`softmax_scale`, `bmm2_scale`→`output_scale`); the adapter uses the new names with unchanged semantics.

## Validation

Rebased onto vLLM main `193d81ab`; measured at `b55821cb` with `flashinfer-python==0.7.4` (PyPI, final release). GB300 nodes with four GPUs each, TP=4/MTP=3, CuTe DSL 4.8.0, PyTorch 2.14 NVIDIA build / CUDA 13.4. The changed CUDA target (`_C_stable_libtorch`) is rebuilt for SM103 over the published native wheel of main ancestor `3b1f19c1` (no native source changes between it and `193d81ab`). All comparisons are PrimTS versus native on this build.

**Local correctness.** 16 adapter tests and 18 fused-producer tests pass, including BF16/FP8 long-KV cases (8K/160K), partial packed requests, inactive requests and CUDA-graph replay against independent FP32 references; numerical references/tolerances are unchanged. All of `tests/models/step5` passes on CUDA (15 passed; 17 ROCm-only skips; `test_mtp_config.py` needs Hugging Face Hub access). Pre-commit passes for the full PR range.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/step5/test_prims_ts_attention.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/test_fused_qknorm_rope_cache.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/step5
```

**Standalone attention.** The PR's own adapter classes at Step5 TP4 per-rank geometry (16 query heads, 1 KV group, head dim 192, page 32, DSA top-k 512 blocks of 8, SWA window 512); cold L2 (1 GiB rewrite before each iteration), CUDA events, median of 50. Decode is CUDA-graph replayed and includes region selection and the head-wise gate; prefill includes selection and the single sparse launch.

| Case (µs) | Native BF16 | PrimTS BF16 | PrimTS FP8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DSA decode B32 Q4, KV 96K | 130.2 | 136.3 | 109.6 |
| DSA decode B64 Q4, KV 96K | 207.9 | 201.8 | 160.9 |
| DSA decode B32 Q4, KV 160K | 138.4 | 142.5 | 117.9 |
| DSA decode B64 Q4, KV 160K | 222.3 | 220.2 | 175.2 |
| DSA prefill 8K chunk, KV 8K | — | 494.0 | 508.2 |
| DSA prefill 8K chunk, KV 160K | — | 2879.1 | 2828.7 |
| SWA prefill 8K chunk | — | 105.9 | 96.9 |
| SWA decode B64 Q4, KV 96K | — | 24.7 | 19.6 |

At B32/B64, PrimTS FP8 decode is 1.17–1.29× faster than native and PrimTS BF16 is 0.96–1.03× native. At B1/B8 PrimTS BF16 is 0.81–0.93× native, which is why BF16 decode routes to PrimTS only at padded batch ≥32. PrimTS BF16 decode matches native BF16 on identical inputs to 0.33–0.38% relative L2 (40 cases measured, including B1/B8 and SWA decode at B1/B32).

**End-to-end serving.** Official `vllm bench serve`, real weights and frozen LongBench Qasper-derived prompts, prefix caching disabled, prefill chunk 8192. One warmup trial excluded, then three measured trials; tables report medians of per-trial means. Input labels are approximate; tokenizer-reported counts are retained. Each backend ran on its own node with the same image and build.

| Backend | 8K/B1 TTFT ms | 160K/B1 TTFT s | 96K input/concurrency32 TTFT s | TPOT ms/token | Output tokens/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Native BF16 | 279.98 | 6.195 | 58.419 | 116.68 | 130.08 |
| PrimTS BF16 | 248.42 (1.13×) | 5.438 (1.14×) | 50.615 (1.15×) | 103.19 (1.13×) | 147.04 (1.13×) |
| PrimTS FP8 | 241.67 (1.16×) | 5.396 (1.15×) | 50.239 (1.16×) | 105.33 (1.11×) | 145.41 (1.12×) |

<details><summary>Trial ranges and same-node PrimTS decode rerun</summary>

Measured concurrency32 TPOT ranges (three trials): native 116.2–117.9, PrimTS BF16 102.3–103.6, PrimTS FP8 104.3–106.3 ms/token; MTP mean acceptance length 1.58 / 1.58 / 1.57.

Because the backends ran on different nodes, both PrimTS backends were rerun back-to-back on one node with warm caches (concurrency32 only): PrimTS FP8 107.28 ms/token (106.0–113.3), 143.25 tokens/s; PrimTS BF16 109.77 ms/token (107.9–115.9), 140.67 tokens/s. The BF16/FP8 TPOT ordering in the main table is within the run-to-run variance of this workload.

</details>

The concurrency32 case generates 512 tokens per request and includes scheduling, ongoing prefill and MTP acceptance effects. It is a serving workload, not an isolated fixed-batch decode-forward measurement.

**Startup and compilation.** Cold: empty per-backend compilation caches. Warm: fresh process reusing that backend's caches. After readiness, prompt lengths 128–16384 run twice; no build occurs after readiness in any probe.

| Backend | Cold readiness s¹ | Warm readiness s¹ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Native BF16 | 1174.9 | not measured |
| PrimTS BF16 | 1270.4 | 278.2 |
| PrimTS FP8 | 1300.9 | 290.2 |

¹ Readiness includes model loading, JIT compilation and graph warmup. Cold startup includes about 310 s of `fused_moe_trtllm_sm100` nvcc JIT in every backend (`flashinfer-jit-cache` not installed).

**Accuracy.** GPQA Diamond, AIME 2024 and GSM8K, one repeat per backend on this build (**4,641 responses**; every request completed). Natural prompts, temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, high reasoning, max_tokens=1,000,000, max_model_len=1,048,576, identical frozen prompts/seeds across backends. Responses here and the previous stack's repeat 0 are scored with the same rule-based answer parser, which under-counts GSM8K relative to the audited extraction below; compare columns, not against that table.

| Dataset | Native | PrimTS BF16 | PrimTS FP8 | Previous stack repeat 0 (native / BF16 / FP8) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPQA Diamond (198) | 91.92% | 92.93% | 91.41% | 88.89% / 93.94% / 90.40% |
| AIME 2024 (30) | 96.67% | 100.00% | 96.67% | 100.00% / 100.00% / 100.00% |
| GSM8K (1319) | 94.54% | 94.31% | 94.69% | 94.54% / 94.01% / 93.78% |

<details><summary>Previous full accuracy campaign (8612c29ed3 + FlashInfer c7f1a3ca, two repeats, audited extraction)</summary>

9,282 responses. A common native BF16 local model extracts every saved response without reference answers; supporting quotations and extraction disagreements are audited. Predictions are frozen before comparison; two GSM8K reference items stated in shoe pairs are converted to individual-shoe units before exact numeric comparison.

| Dataset | Questions/repeat | Native | PrimTS BF16 | PrimTS FP8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPQA Diamond | 198 | 92.93% | 93.43% | 90.66% |
| AIME 2024 | 30 | 100.00% | 98.33% | 98.33% |
| GSM8K | 1319 | 97.04% | 96.97% | 96.82% |

| Dataset | Native repeat 0 / repeat 1 | PrimTS BF16 repeat 0 / repeat 1 | PrimTS FP8 repeat 0 / repeat 1 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPQA Diamond | 178 of 198 / 190 of 198 | 187 of 198 / 183 of 198 | 178 of 198 / 181 of 198 |
| AIME 2024 | 30 of 30 / 30 of 30 | 30 of 30 / 29 of 30 | 30 of 30 / 29 of 30 |
| GSM8K | 1281 of 1319 / 1279 of 1319 | 1278 of 1319 / 1280 of 1319 | 1277 of 1319 / 1277 of 1319 |

FP8 GPQA was 2.27 percentage points below native in that two-repeat campaign; these results do not establish accuracy equivalence.

</details>

## Details

Enable with `--kernel-config '{"step5_attention_backend":"prims_ts"}'` and `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` or `fp8_e4m3`. Block size 32; MTP=3 means three draft tokens plus one target token (Q=4). Query dtype follows backend/cache configuration independently of batch routing.

Hardware validation covers GB300/SM103. SM100/107 remain untested locally, and H200 CI cannot execute the PrimTS adapter cases. No duplicate Step5 PrimTS integration exists in pinned main; existing integrations for other models are distinct. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support --tokens-only
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The Rust frontend rejects `--tokens-only` as unsupported. This makes it behave as the Python frontend does:

- Accepts `--tokens-only` on `vllm-rs serve` and through the launcher's `--args-json`.
- Implies `--enable-scale-out`, so the scale-out routes, including `/inference/v1/generate`, are registered even with an explicit `--enable-scale-out false`, matching Python's dedicated mode in `scale_out/factories.py`.
- Implies `--skip-tokenizer-init`, as Python's `EngineArgs.tokens_only` does: the Rust frontend loads no tokenizer, and the managed Python engine that standalone `vllm-rs serve` launches receives `--skip-tokenizer-init`. The Python-first path sends `tokens_only` without `skip_tokenizer_init` (Python sets it on the model config only), so Rust derives it itself.

Both frontends already implement these two flags, so `--tokens-only` is resolved into them in `SharedRuntimeArgs`, which the `serve` and `--args-json` paths share; the server sees no new option. Without a tokenizer, the existing checks return the 400s Python returns: stop strings fail with "stop strings require detokenization", and `output_mode="text"` with "requires a tokenizer".

Divergence: Python also registers an unauthenticated legacy `/abort_requests` alias under `--tokens-only` for existing deployments. The Rust frontend does not; use `/inference/v1/abort_requests`, which serves the same handler behind `--api-key`.

## Duplicate check

No open PR adds `--tokens-only` to the Rust frontend (searched "rust tokens-only" and "rust abort_requests"). #63461 implements `/inference/v1/abort_requests`; this PR doesn't touch that handler.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-server --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run -p vllm-cmd
```

New test: `tokens_only_implies_scale_out_and_skip_tokenizer_init`: through `serve` (with an explicit `--enable-scale-out false`) and through `--args-json` (with `skip_tokenizer_init: false`), the config has the scale-out routes on and no tokenizer, and the managed engine receives `--skip-tokenizer-init`.

`test_stop_strings_rejected_when_tokens_only` and `test_text_mode_rejected_when_tokens_only` in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py` now run against the Rust frontend.

## Test Result

- `vllm-cmd`: 123 passed. Removing either implication fails the new test.
- fmt and clippy are clean.
- The two tokens-only tests on a GB200 with Qwen3-0.6B: Rust frontend 2 passed, Python frontend 2 passed; with `vllm-rs` built from `main`, both fail at startup (`tokens_only` is not implemented).

AI assistance (Cursor agent) was used; I reviewed every changed line. The follow-up commit replacing the route-level implementation with the flag resolution was written with Claude Code and reviewed by @BugenZhao.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Make early prefill abort cleanup idempotent
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make Mooncake prefill abort cleanup idempotent when the producer worker has no send record yet, so one missing record does not stop cleanup of the rest of the batch. This is separate from #50565, which handles a Decode-side stale receive completion after an early abort.

## Claims

- An abort that reaches `record_send_reqs` before a transfer record exists, or after that record was already removed, no longer raises `KeyError`.
- Records that are present keep the existing assertion that `ready` is not set. Cleanup does not cancel or drain an in-flight Mooncake transfer.

## Validation

Rebased onto `main` (`176a74c8e0`). CPU connector tests, using the cached `facebook/opt-125m` config with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py -m cpu_test -q
```

Result: **10 passed, 160 deselected**.

`test_prefill_early_abort_cleanup_is_idempotent` calls the worker's `record_send_reqs` directly. The worker holds one record that is aborted and one unrelated record, and the abort batch also names a transfer that was never recorded. The same batch is applied twice, so the second call repeats the abort after the record is gone. Both calls must leave only the unrelated record. On `main` the test fails with `KeyError`. No GPU, RDMA, or server run; the change does not alter transfer bytes.

## Details

On the prefill scheduler, a request that finishes for a reason other than `FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED` is added to `reqs_not_processed` and is not queued for send. The worker then does `reqs_need_send.pop(transfer_id)`. That record is created only after allocation metadata arrives, so an abort before that point, or a repeated abort after the first pop, raises `KeyError` and skips later ids in the same batch.

`pop(transfer_id, None)` treats a missing record as already removed. If a record is present, it still must not be `ready`. Sending counters are unchanged, and this does not reclaim unknown transfer placeholders or cancel an active transfer.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Serve /inference/v1/abort_requests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend answers `POST /inference/v1/abort_requests` with a 501 placeholder. This serves it with the Python frontend's contract, so a scale-out router can abort in-flight `/inference/v1/generate` requests on a Rust-fronted server.

This is a reimplementation of the scope of #63461 (draft), written without its code; @WeiHanTu is credited as co-author.

## Claims

- `/inference/v1/abort_requests` is served behind the scale-out gate (`--enable-scale-out`, 403 otherwise) and `--api-key`, like `/inference/v1/generate`.
- Same request contract as Python (`token_in_token_out/api_router.py`): the body is parsed as JSON whatever its `Content-Type`; `request_ids` is a required string or list of strings, otherwise 400; the IDs are the `request_id`s that generate returns; unknown IDs and an empty list abort nothing; the response is an empty 200.
- An aborted generate stream ends with a chunk carrying `finish_reason: "abort"`.
- `test_stream_delivers_abort_finish_chunk` (`tokens` and `text`) and `test_abort_requests_is_served_without_tokens_only` now run against the Rust frontend.

## Validation

```bash
cd rust
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy -p vllm-server --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run -p vllm-server --all-features --locked
```

- `vllm-server`: 692 passed. New route tests against the scripted mock engine:
  - `scale_out_abort_requests_validates_body`: seven body and `Content-Type` cases (snapshot).
  - `scale_out_abort_requests_finishes_generate_stream`: an empty list and an unknown ID leave the stream running; aborting the returned ID sends one abort to the engine and ends the stream with `[] "abort"`.
  - Each fails when the route is pointed back at the 501 placeholder; the stream test also fails without the empty-list guard.
- Rust frontend on a GB200, Qwen3-0.6B, `vllm-rs` built from this branch:

  ```bash
  cd tests
  VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH=<vllm-rs> \
    pytest -v entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py -k abort
  ```

  ```
  test_serving_tokens.py::test_stream_delivers_abort_finish_chunk[tokens] PASSED
  test_serving_tokens.py::test_stream_delivers_abort_finish_chunk[text] PASSED
  test_serving_tokens.py::test_abort_requests_is_served_without_tokens_only PASSED
  ====================== 3 passed, 27 deselected in 56.43s =======================
  ```

## Details

- The handler shares only `abort` (by external request ID) with the dev-mode `/abort_requests`, whose contract differs: there, a missing or empty `request_ids` aborts every request. Because `abort(&[])` means "all", the new handler skips the call for an empty list, as the gRPC `Abort` handler does.
- Differences from Python:
  - Python aborts in a background task after answering 200. Rust awaits the abort, which finalizes the local streams and sends one message to the engine, so a failed send to the engine returns 500 instead of being logged.
  - Validation messages use serde's wording, and `param` is `null`.
- Python also serves an unauthenticated `/abort_requests` alias under `--tokens-only` for existing deployments. The Rust frontend does not serve it; use this route.
- Duplicate check: #63461 (draft) covers the same route. This PR reimplements it independently instead of building on that branch, and credits its author.
